input.content:
# Real-to-Sim Correction Data Collection Protocol

**Status:** Draft 2026-05-16. Each recording session requires Article II
human approval to execute; this document is the plan, not authorization.

---

## Purpose

Stage 1 baseline (`docs/stage_1_baseline.md`) leaves the simulator-only
classifier at **50% sensitivity / 44% FP** on real bathroom CSVs.
Further simulator tweaking without real data hits diminishing returns
(also documented in the baseline). To close the gap, every simulator
component needs to be **fit against real ground truth**.

This protocol specifies what real measurements to collect, in what
order, and exactly which simulator parameter each measurement corrects.

The "tap test" is one piece of this (the IR-fitting piece); the full
plan covers tap + walk + drop + fall-surrogate + noise so a single
bathroom deployment captures everything needed.

---

## Real-to-sim correction map

This is the single most important table in this document. Each row is
a measurement type, what simulator component it fits, and the residual
that quantifies success.

| Measurement | Simulator component it fits | Fit method | Acceptance residual |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tap IR at 3 distances** | `signals.py` floor-plate FEA (`floor_sim` damping ζ_plate, modal density, spatial decay coefficient `REAL_TO_SIM_SCALE`) + sensor-model end-to-end gain | Compare measured tap IR (envelope + spectrum) to simulated tap IR at same distance; minimize log-spectral distance + ringdown-tau residual | Per-tap envelope correlation ≥ 0.85; ringdown τ within ±30% |
| **Quiet baseline (60 s)** | `signals.py` `bg_environmental_noise` ASD (peaks + 1/f + white) — already done once, redo per bathroom | Compute Welch PSD of real baseline, overwrite per-peak amplitudes in noise model | Real PSD vs sim PSD within ±6 dB across 1–500 Hz |
| **Calibration walk (60 s)** | `signals.py` `_footstep_force_profile` (peak force range, contact time) | Match measured per-step peak amplitude distribution and footstep cadence distribution | Peak amplitude mean within ±20%; cadence distribution KS-test p > 0.05 |
| **Object drops × {phone, glass, water-bottle} × 3 distances** | `signals.py` `drop_trajectory` (`rebound_pattern` parameters: COR, multi-impact spacing) | Match measured multi-peak count, inter-peak interval, decay envelope | Multi-peak count match ±1; decay envelope correlation ≥ 0.80 |
| **Catfood-bag drops × 3 distances × {body-in-path, no-body}** | `signals.py` `fall_trajectory` `body_absorption_db` (currently 5 dB, weakly validated) | Compare amplitude ratio (body-in-path vs not) to current 5 dB assumption | Amplitude ratio within ±2 dB of measurement |
| **Slow-slump surrogate (heavy bag lowered onto floor)** | `signals.py` `fall_slump` profile (slow-rumble onset + final impact two-stage signature) | Match measured pre-impact slow build + impact decay shape | Two-stage signature visually matches in plot review (qualitative for now) |
| **Confuser noise (shower, vent, flush, washer if present)** | `signals.py` noise-profile amplitudes for `noise_shower`, `noise_vent`, etc. | Match per-source PSD against current noise-profile amplitudes | Per-source PSD within ±6 dB across 1–500 Hz |

After each fit, the **acceptance test for the corrected simulator** is
sim-to-real v3: rerun `scripts/sim_to_real_test_v2.py` on the held-out
events from the *same* bathroom and confirm:
- Sensitivity ≥ 80% (up from 50%)
- FP rate ≤ 10% (down from 44%)

Hitting these on the training bathroom is the **trigger for the 1-bathroom
→ 3-bathroom expand decision** (see Scope below).

---

## Scope: 1 bathroom now, explicit 3-bathroom trigger

Per 2026-05-16 user decision: collect the full protocol on **1 bathroom
first** before deciding whether to expand. This validates the protocol
itself before front-loading multi-bathroom logistics.

**Trigger to expand to 3 bathrooms:**

Expand if **any** of the following is true after corrected simulator
is tested on the 1-bathroom data:

1. **Sim-to-real v3 hits the 80%/10% target on the training bathroom**
   → the correction worked on this bathroom; need 2 more bathrooms to
   prove it generalizes (otherwise we may have just over-fit to one tile)
2. **Sim-to-real v3 fails by a *small* margin** (e.g., 70%/15%) → the
   simulator structure looks OK but more data is needed; collect 2 more
   bathrooms with the same protocol
3. **Tap-test repeatability is poor on a single bathroom** (per-tap
   envelope correlation < 0.7 across 5 repeats at the same distance) →
   sensor mount or tile-coupling is inconsistent; expand to characterize
   variance source before drawing conclusions

**Stay at 1 bathroom only if:**

- Sim-to-real v3 fails by a *large* margin (e.g., < 60%/> 25%) — extra
  data won't fix a structurally wrong simulator; instead, draft Bills to
  revise the simulator's structural assumptions (e.g., add multi-tile
  mosaic modeling, revisit FEA mode selection)

The trigger is recorded here so the decision is pre-committed and not
post-rationalized.

---

## Hardware setup

- **Device under test:** STM32F103C8T6 + MiniSense 100 in the
  ground_cantilever_housing (CAD: `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/`)
- **Preload:** ~200 g weight on top platform (loose, not bonded)
- **Firmware:** active build at `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/代码 - 调节发送频率/USER/main.c`
  with **INT_MARK = 0** (mandatory — satisfies Amendment 1 P1 ≥ 1 kHz
  rate floor per Case 1+2)
- **Transport:** USART2 (PA2/PA3, 115200 baud, FireWater ASCII `%.3f\n`),
  via USB-serial adapter
- **Logging host:** laptop / Pi recording UART → CSV

**Sample-rate check before any recording:** capture 10 s of UART
output, compute measured_rate_hz = lines / wall-clock-elapsed. Must be
≥ 1000 Hz. If less, abort — INT_MARK is wrong, transport is buffering,
or the firmware build is the wrong one.

**Mandatory CSV metadata header** (per Case 1 ruling, missing →
not admissible as Article I evidence):

```
# int_mark: 0
# transport: USART2_USB
# measured_rate_hz: 1380
# bathroom_id: bathroom_A
# tile_size_mm: 200x200
# device_xy_in_room: "0.3m from west wall, 0.5m from south wall"
# preload_mass_g: 200
# operator: shiyao
# date: 2026-05-XX
# session_id: 001
# measurement_type: tap_0.5m  # or baseline / walk / drop_phone_1.5m / etc.
```

---

## Pre-session mount sanity check (~1 min, every session)

Catches a bad deploy before wasting 30+ minutes on data that's
contaminated by a compliant contact.

1. Place housing on tile. Confirm baseplate flush, no rocking when
   pushing the cap with a finger.
2. Place 200 g weight on top platform.
3. Start UART capture.
4. Tap the tile 30 cm from housing with a fingernail. 5 taps, ~2 s apart.
5. Stop capture. Plot or scope:
   - **Pass:** clean impulse, ringdown < 50 ms, no oscillation between taps
   - **Fail:** ringdown > 200 ms (compliant contact), delayed rise (foam
     in path), or large oscillation between taps (loose preload / rocking
     baseplate)

If fail: alcohol-wipe the tile, re-seat the housing, repeat. Don't
proceed to data collection until sanity check passes.

---

## Per-bathroom protocol

### Phase A — Install calibration (~5 min)

Same as `docs/device_context.md` Install-Time Calibration Design.
Produces the per-bathroom calibration reference that the algorithm
will use at deploy time.

| Step | Duration | File | Purpose |
|------|----------|------|---------|
| A1: Quiet baseline | 60 s, no one in room | `<bathroom_id>_baseline.csv` | Noise PSD reference; SNR denominator |
| A2: Tap at 0.5 m | 5 taps, ~2 s apart | `<bathroom_id>_tap_0.5m.csv` | IR at near distance |
| A3: Tap at 1.5 m | 5 taps | `<bathroom_id>_tap_1.5m.csv` | IR at mid distance |
| A4: Tap at 2.5 m | 5 taps | `<bathroom_id>_tap_2.5m.csv` | IR at far distance |
| A5: Calibration walk | 60 s normal walking | `<bathroom_id>_walk.csv` | Footstep amplitude reference |

Mark tap locations with tape so they're repeatable for re-installs.

### Phase B — Sim-correction data (15–30 min)

Each event in this phase is **labeled in a separate paper / phone log**
with timestamp, class, distance, and any anomaly (bounce off wall, wet
floor, etc.).

| Event class | Count target | Distances | Notes |
|-------------|--------------|-----------|-------|
| Object drop — water bottle | 15 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 5 each | Rigid, single-impact-with-rebound class. Drops from waist height (~1 m). |
| Object drop — phone | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × ~3 each | Lower-mass rigid object. Same drop height. |
| Object drop — glass | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | Brittle / multi-impact class. Drops from waist height. Be careful. |
| Catfood-bag drop (body-fall surrogate) | 30 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 10 each | At 1.5 m, split 5 with operator between drop and sensor ("body in path") and 5 without |
| Slow-slump surrogate | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | Heavy bag (~10 kg) lowered slowly onto floor; controlled descent, not free fall |
| Step / walk (extra, beyond A5) | continuous 5 min | n/a | Operator walks varied paths; oversample for cadence statistics |
| Confuser — shower running | 60 s | n/a | Continuous, separately recorded |
| Confuser — vent on | 60 s | n/a | Continuous |
| Confuser — toilet flush | 5 flushes | n/a | One file with 5 distinct flushes |
| Confuser — washer (if present) | 60 s + a spin-up | n/a | Skip if not in/adjacent to bathroom |

Save Phase B events grouped by class:
```
<bathroom_id>_drop_water_<date>.csv      # all water drops in one file
<bathroom_id>_drop_phone_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_drop_glass_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_fall_catfood_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_fall_slump_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_walk_extra_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_shower_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_vent_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_flush_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_washer_<date>.csv
```

### Logging discipline

For every event in Phase B:
- Note timestamp (CSV records its own; phone log records wall clock for
  cross-reference)
- Event class label
- Distance from sensor (m)
- Body-in-path? (yes/no) — relevant for catfood-bag drops at 1.5 m
- Surface state (wet/dry)
- Any anomaly

A handwritten or phone-notes log with timestamps is sufficient. Goal:
ability to retro-label each event in the CSV during post-processing.

---

## Output layout

Per bathroom:
```
data/<bathroom_id>/
├── <bathroom_id>_baseline_<date>.csv      # Phase A1
├── <bathroom_id>_tap_0.5m_<date>.csv      # Phase A2
├── <bathroom_id>_tap_1.5m_<date>.csv      # Phase A3
├── <bathroom_id>_tap_2.5m_<date>.csv      # Phase A4
├── <bathroom_id>_walk_<date>.csv          # Phase A5
├── <bathroom_id>_drop_water_<date>.csv    # Phase B
├── <bathroom_id>_drop_phone_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_drop_glass_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_fall_catfood_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_fall_slump_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_walk_extra_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_shower_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_vent_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_flush_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_washer_<date>.csv  # if applicable
└── <bathroom_id>_log.md                    # human label log
```

Storage: the CSVs are likely large (kHz × minutes × float). Recommend
`data/` outside the repo with a symlink, and `data/` in `.gitignore`,
unless individual files stay under ~5 MB.

The existing CSVs in `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/bathroom_testing/`
(catfood_201505, water_201505, step_201505) should be migrated under
`data/bathroom_legacy/` with metadata headers retro-fitted (operator
best-effort: int_mark and measured_rate_hz are the load-bearing fields).

---

## How each measurement updates the simulator

This is the "what changes in `src/signals.py`" half of the loop. After
data is collected, draft a single **Bill** ("Sim-to-real v3 corrections
from bathroom_A data") covering all simulator parameter changes derived
from the data. The Bill goes through the standard Judicial Process — no
silent simulator parameter changes.

| Real measurement | Simulator parameter | Recommended fitting script |
|---|---|---|
| Tap IR per distance | `floor_sim` damping ζ, `REAL_TO_SIM_SCALE` | `scripts/fit_floor_ir.py` (to write) |
| Quiet baseline PSD | `bg_environmental_noise` peak amplitudes | `scripts/fit_noise_psd.py` (extend existing real_noise_spectrum work) |
| Calibration + extra walk | `_footstep_force_profile` peak range, contact time distribution | `scripts/fit_footstep.py` (to write) |
| Object drops (water/phone/glass) | `drop_trajectory` COR + multi-impact spacing per `rebound_pattern` | `scripts/fit_drop_rebound.py` (to write) |
| Catfood drops body-in vs out | `fall_trajectory` `body_absorption_db` (currently 5 dB guess) | `scripts/fit_body_absorption.py` (to write) |
| Confuser noise | `noise_shower` / `noise_vent` / `noise_flush` amplitudes | `scripts/fit_confuser_noise.py` (to write) |

These fit scripts don't exist yet — they get drafted as part of the
Bill execution, not preemptively. Listed here so the data-collection
plan and the analysis plan are visible together.

---

## Open questions before first execution

1. **Tap source standardization:** finger-nail tap is operator-dependent
   (amplitude varies ±50%). For better repeatability, recommend a
   **calibrated drop** — e.g., a 10 g steel ball dropped from a fixed
   100 mm height through a vertical guide. Build a simple jig before
   Phase A2–A4. (Optional refinement; finger taps are usable for an
   initial pass to validate the protocol.)
2. **Sample-rate measurement:** one-shot 10 s capture per session, or
   inline timestamp in CSV header? Recommend: inline, record session
   wall-clock start and CSV row count, derive rate post-hoc.
3. **Storage path:** `data/` symlinked outside repo with `.gitignore`,
   or in-repo if CSVs stay small? Recommend: symlinked, decide once we
   see actual file sizes.
4. **Legacy CSV admission:** retro-fitted metadata is operator-attested
   not measured. Acceptable for Phase B comparison but flag the
   asymmetry in any v3 report.
5. **Sample-event-segmentation tool:** Phase B produces hour-long CSVs
   with discrete events. Need a tool (script or simple GUI) to mark
   event windows from the log file. Build alongside Phase B execution.

## Pre-session mount sanity check (~1 min, every session)

Catches a bad deploy before wasting 30+ minutes on data that's
contaminated by a compliant contact.

1. Place housing on tile. Confirm baseplate flush, no rocking when
   pushing the cap with a finger.
2. Place 200 g weight on top platform.
3. Start UART capture.
4. Tap the tile 30 cm from housing with a fingernail. 5 taps, ~2 s apart.
5. Stop capture. Plot or scope:
   - **Pass:** clean impulse, ringdown < 50 ms, no oscillation between taps
   - **Fail:** ringdown > 200 ms (compliant contact), delayed rise (foam
     in path), or large oscillation between taps (loose preload / rocking
     baseplate)

If fail: alcohol-wipe the tile, re-seat the housing, repeat. Don't
proceed to data collection until sanity check passes.

---

## Per-bathroom protocol

### Phase A — Install calibration (~5 min)

Same as `docs/device_context.md` Install-Time Calibration Design.
Produces the per-bathroom calibration reference that the algorithm
will use at deploy time.

| Step | Duration | File | Purpose |
|------|----------|------|---------|
| A1: Quiet baseline | 60 s, no one in room | `<bathroom_id>_baseline.csv` | Noise PSD reference; SNR denominator |
| A2: Tap at 0.5 m | 5 taps, ~2 s apart | `<bathroom_id>_tap_0.5m.csv` | IR at near distance |
| A3: Tap at 1.5 m | 5 taps | `<bathroom_id>_tap_1.5m.csv` | IR at mid distance |
| A4: Tap at 2.5 m | 5 taps | `<bathroom_id>_tap_2.5m.csv` | IR at far distance |
| A5: Calibration walk | 60 s normal walking | `<bathroom_id>_walk.csv` | Footstep amplitude reference |

Mark tap locations with tape so they're repeatable for re-installs.

### Phase B — Sim-correction data (15–30 min)

Each event in this phase is **labeled in a separate paper / phone log**
with timestamp, class, distance, and any anomaly (bounce off wall, wet
floor, etc.).

| Event class | Count target | Distances | Notes |
|-------------|--------------|-----------|-------|
| Object drop — water bottle | 15 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 5 each | Rigid, single-impact-with-rebound class. Drops from waist height (~1 m). |
| Object drop — phone | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × ~3 each | Lower-mass rigid object. Same drop height. |
| Object drop — glass | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | Brittle / multi-impact class. Drops from waist height. Be careful. |
| Catfood-bag drop (body-fall surrogate) | 30 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 10 each | At 1.5 m, split 5 with operator between drop and sensor ("body in path") and 5 without |
| Slow-slump surrogate | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | Heavy bag (~10 kg) lowered slowly onto floor; controlled descent, not free fall |
| Step / walk (extra, beyond A5) | continuous 5 min | n/a | Operator walks varied paths; oversample for cadence statistics |
| Confuser — shower running | 60 s | n/a | Continuous, separately recorded |
| Confuser — vent on | 60 s | n/a | Continuous |
| Confuser — toilet flush | 5 flushes | n/a | One file with 5 distinct flushes |
| Confuser — washer (if present) | 60 s + a spin-up | n/a | Skip if not in/adjacent to bathroom |

Save Phase B events grouped by class:
```
<bathroom_id>_drop_water_<date>.csv      # all water drops in one file
<bathroom_id>_drop_phone_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_drop_glass_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_fall_catfood_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_fall_slump_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_walk_extra_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_shower_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_vent_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_flush_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_noise_washer_<date>.csv
```

### Logging discipline

For every event in Phase B:
- Note timestamp (CSV records its own; phone log records wall clock for
  cross-reference)
- Event class label
- Distance from sensor (m)
- Body-in-path? (yes/no) — relevant for catfood-bag drops at 1.5 m
- Surface state (wet/dry)
- Any anomaly

A handwritten or phone-notes log with timestamps is sufficient. Goal:
ability to retro-label each event in the CSV during post-processing.

---

## Output layout

Per bathroom:
```
data/<bathroom_id>/
├── <bathroom_id>_baseline_<date>.csv      # Phase A1
├── <bathroom_id>_tap_0.5m_<date>.csv      # Phase A2
├── <bathroom_id>_tap_1.5m_<date>.csv      # Phase A3
├── <bathroom_id>_tap_2.5m_<date>.csv      # Phase A4
├── <bathroom_id>_walk_<date>.csv          # Phase A5
├── <bathroom_id>_drop_water_<date>.csv    # Phase B
├── <bathroom_id>_drop_phone_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_drop_glass_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_fall_catfood_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_fall_slump_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_walk_extra_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_shower_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_vent_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_flush_<date>.csv
├── <bathroom_id>_noise_washer_<date>.csv  # if applicable
└── <bathroom_id>_log.md                    # human label log
```

Storage: the CSVs are likely large (kHz × minutes × float). Recommend
`data/` outside the repo with a symlink, and `data/` in `.gitignore`,
unless individual files stay under ~5 MB.

The existing CSVs in `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/bathroom_testing/`
(catfood_201505, water_201505, step_201505) should be migrated under
`data/bathroom_legacy/` with metadata headers retro-fitted (operator
best-effort: int_mark and measured_rate_hz are the load-bearing fields).

---

## How each measurement updates the simulator

This is the "what changes in `src/signals.py`" half of the loop. After
data is collected, draft a single **Bill** ("Sim-to-real v3 corrections
from bathroom_A data") covering all simulator parameter changes derived
from the data. The Bill goes through the standard Judicial Process — no
silent simulator parameter changes.

| Real measurement | Simulator parameter | Recommended fitting script |
|---|---|---|
| Tap IR per distance | `floor_sim` damping ζ, `REAL_TO_SIM_SCALE` | `scripts/fit_floor_ir.py` (to write) |
| Quiet baseline PSD | `bg_environmental_noise` peak amplitudes | `scripts/fit_noise_psd.py` (extend existing real_noise_spectrum work) |
| Calibration + extra walk | `_footstep_force_profile` peak range, contact time distribution | `scripts/fit_footstep.py` (to write) |
| Object drops (water/phone/glass) | `drop_trajectory` COR + multi-impact spacing per `rebound_pattern` | `scripts/fit_drop_rebound.py` (to write) |
| Catfood drops body-in vs out | `fall_trajectory` `body_absorption_db` (currently 5 dB guess) | `scripts/fit_body_absorption.py` (to write) |
| Confuser noise | `noise_shower` / `noise_vent` / `noise_flush` amplitudes | `scripts/fit_confuser_noise.py` (to write) |

These fit scripts don't exist yet — they get drafted as part of the
Bill execution, not preemptively. Listed here so the data-collection
plan and the analysis plan are visible together.

---

## Open questions before first execution

1. **Tap source standardization:** finger-nail tap is operator-dependent
   (amplitude varies ±50%). For better repeatability, recommend a
   **calibrated drop** — e.g., a 10 g steel ball dropped from a fixed
   100 mm height through a vertical guide. Build a simple jig before
   Phase A2–A4. (Optional refinement; finger taps are usable for an
   initial pass to validate the protocol.)
2. **Sample-rate measurement:** one-shot 10 s capture per session, or
   inline timestamp in CSV header? Recommend: inline, record session
   wall-clock start and CSV row count, derive rate post-hoc.
3. **Storage path:** `data/` symlinked outside repo with `.gitignore`,
   or in-repo if CSVs stay small? Recommend: symlinked, decide once we
   see actual file sizes.
4. **Legacy CSV admission:** retro-fitted metadata is operator-attested
   not measured. Acceptable for Phase B comparison but flag the
   asymmetry in any v3 report.
5. **Sample-event-segmentation tool:** Phase B produces hour-long CSVs
   with discrete events. Need a tool (script or simple GUI) to mark
   event windows from the log file. Build alongside Phase B execution.

# Data Collection Protocol — Stage 1 → Stage 2 Bridge

**Status:** Draft 2026-05-16. Approved-to-execute pending Article II
human go-ahead on each session (each recording session is a Stage 2
gate prerequisite, not a Standing Order).

**Purpose:** Bridge Stage 1's simulator-only baseline (50% sensitivity /
44% FP per `docs/stage_1_baseline.md`) to a real-data corpus that
Stage 2 can train and validate against.

This protocol bundles three things that share the same hardware setup,
so you only deploy the device once per session:

1. **Mount sanity check** (per-session, ~1 min) — confirms the housing
   is properly seated on the tile
2. **Install-time calibration capture** (per-bathroom, ~5 min) — the
   3-step calibration in `docs/device_context.md` Install-Time
   Calibration Design
3. **Labeled event collection** (per-bathroom, 15–60 min) — the actual
   training/validation data

---

## Hardware

- **Device under test:** STM32F103C8T6 + MiniSense 100 in the
  ground_cantilever_housing (CAD: `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/`)
- **Preload:** ~200 g weight on top platform
- **Firmware:** active build at `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/代码 - 调节发送频率/USER/main.c`
  with **INT_MARK = 0** (mandatory — satisfies Amendment 1 P1 ≥ 1 kHz
  rate floor per Case 1+2)
- **Transport:** USB-USART2 (USART2 PA2/PA3, 115200 baud, FireWater
  ASCII `%.3f\n`)
- **Sample-rate check:** before any recording, capture 10 s of UART
  output, count lines, compute measured_rate_hz. Must be ≥ 1000 Hz
  per Amendment 1 P1. If less, abort — INT_MARK is wrong or buffer
  is dropping.

**Mandatory CSV metadata** (per Case 1 ruling, CSVs missing these are
**not admissible as Article I evidence**):

```
# int_mark: 0
# transport: USART2_USB
# measured_rate_hz: <actual measured rate, e.g. 1380>
# bathroom_id: <e.g. "bathroom_A_main">
# tile_size_mm: <approx, e.g. 200x200>
# device_xy_in_room: <e.g. "0.3m from west wall, 0.5m from south wall">
# operator: <name>
# date: YYYY-MM-DD
# session_id: <unique>
```

---

## Session 0: Per-session mount sanity check (~1 min)

Goal: catch a bad deploy before wasting 30 minutes on a session that
turns out to have a compliant contact.

1. Place housing on tile. Confirm baseplate is flush — no rocking when
   you push the cap with a finger.
2. Place 200 g weight on top platform.
3. Start UART capture.
4. **Tap test:** with a fingernail or pencil eraser, tap the tile
   30 cm from the housing. Repeat 5 times with ~2 s between taps.
5. Stop capture. Visually inspect (plot or scope):
   - **Pass:** clean impulse, ringdown < 50 ms, no visible oscillation
     between taps
   - **Fail (re-seat):** ringdown > 200 ms (compliant contact), or
     delayed rise (foam in path), or large oscillation between taps
     (loose preload or rocking baseplate)

If the sanity check fails, re-clean the tile surface (alcohol wipe,
remove dust/wax), re-seat the housing, repeat.

---

## Session 1: Install-time calibration (~5 min, once per bathroom)

Per `docs/device_context.md` Install-Time Calibration Design.

### Step 1A: Quiet baseline (60 s)

- Operator leaves bathroom, no water running
- Record 60 s of UART
- Save as `<bathroom_id>_baseline_<YYYYMMDD>.csv`
- Purpose: noise floor RMS + spectrum (vent, plumbing, distant
  appliances), becomes the SNR denominator

### Step 1B: Tap test at 3 distances (~2 min)

For each distance ∈ {0.5 m, 1.5 m, 2.5 m} from sensor:
- Mark the tap location with tape so it's repeatable
- Operator stands at that distance, taps floor 5 times with a fingertip,
  ~2 s between taps
- Save as `<bathroom_id>_tap_<distance>m_<YYYYMMDD>.csv`
- Purpose: impulse response per distance → plate damping, spatial
  decay rate, local tile resonance, bonding state

### Step 1C: Calibration walk (~1 min)

- Operator walks normally around the bathroom for 60 s, varying paths
- Save as `<bathroom_id>_walk_<YYYYMMDD>.csv`
- Purpose: real footstep signature → reference amplitude for "normal
  walking" used by adaptive thresholds

---

## Session 2: Labeled event collection (15–60 min, repeat per bathroom)

### Event classes to collect (per `docs/device_context.md` Simulation Profile Catalog)

| Class | Event | Target count per bathroom | Notes |
|-------|-------|---------------------------|-------|
| **fall** | catfood-bag drop, body-fall surrogate | ≥ 30 events | At each of 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m, both with and without body-in-path between drop and sensor (per drop-human-sensor finding) |
| **fall** | slow-slump surrogate (heavy bag lowered onto floor) | ≥ 10 events | Slow controlled descent, not free fall |
| **fall** | actual human fall (controlled — onto mat, by operator) | as many as you're willing | Highest-value data. Mat reduces injury but distorts signal — flag mat-cushioned events in metadata. |
| confuser | normal step (walking) | ≥ 30 events (built into walk in 1C) | |
| confuser | water bottle drop (rigid object) | ≥ 15 events at 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | |
| confuser | object drop — phone | ≥ 10 events | Same distances |
| confuser | object drop — glass (be careful) | ≥ 10 events | Same distances |
| confuser | walk-in / walk-out (operator entering/leaving) | ≥ 5 transitions | |
| noise | shower running | 60 s continuous | |
| noise | vent on | 60 s continuous | |
| noise | toilet flush | 5 flushes | |
| noise | washer (if in or adjacent to bathroom) | 60 s + spin-up/spin-down | |

### Logging discipline

For each event during recording:
- Operator says event name out loud immediately at impact (optional —
  helps when manually segmenting later)
- After each event-block, record:
  - Event class label
  - Distance from sensor (m)
  - Body-in-path? (yes/no)
  - Surface state (wet/dry)
  - Any anomaly (e.g., bottle bounced off wall first)

A simple paper or phone-notes log with timestamps is sufficient. The
goal is to be able to label each event in the CSV after the session.

---

## Output

Per bathroom, expected files:
```
<bathroom_id>_baseline_<date>.csv          # Session 1A
<bathroom_id>_tap_0.5m_<date>.csv          # Session 1B
<bathroom_id>_tap_1.5m_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_tap_2.5m_<date>.csv
<bathroom_id>_walk_<date>.csv              # Session 1C
<bathroom_id>_events_<session_n>_<date>.csv  # Session 2 — can be split across runs
<bathroom_id>_log.md                        # event-label log (handwritten OK)
```

Store under `data/<bathroom_id>/` in this repo. Each CSV must include
the metadata header block specified above.

---

## Stage 2 entry criteria (what "enough data" means)

Stage 2 can open when:
- At least 1 bathroom has full install-calibration + ≥ 60 labeled
  events across the catalog (≥ 30 fall surrogates, ≥ 30 confusers)
- All CSVs include the mandatory metadata header
- A held-out test set is identified (e.g., 1 of 3 bathrooms reserved
  for final evaluation, never seen by classifier training)

The classifier retraining + sim-to-real v3 happens after this gate.
A Bill drafted at Stage 2 entry will propose the specific train/val/test
split and the simulator changes (if any) needed once real data exposes
the actual gaps in the synthetic distribution.

---

## What is NOT in scope for this protocol

- **Actual unassisted human falls** — too dangerous outside a controlled
  setting. The catfood-bag and bag-lowering surrogates plus mat-cushioned
  controlled falls cover the simulator's "fall" class.
- **Multi-occupant scenarios** — Stage 3 or later.
- **Multi-bathroom IRL generalization test** — Stage 3.
- **Long-duration unattended recording** — Stage 3 (need a separate
  storage / battery review first).

---

## Open questions before first execution

1. **Sample-rate measurement procedure**: should the rate-check be a
   one-shot count on a dedicated 10 s capture, or inline metadata on
   every recording? (Recommend: inline — record start/stop wall clock
   timestamps + line count in CSV header.)
2. **Storage path:** create `data/` directory in this repo, or store
   outside the repo (large CSVs may bloat git)? Recommend: store outside
   repo, symlink, .gitignore the symlink target.
3. **Backup:** the catfood/water/step CSVs from `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/bathroom_testing/`
   should be migrated into the same `data/` tree with metadata headers
   retro-fitted (operator best-effort) so they're admissible.

Real-to-Sim Correction — Data Collection Protocol

Source: docs/data_collection_protocol.md (committed 2026-05-16, 91b0a5f). This HTML is a reading rendition with experimental-control highlights added — the markdown is the canonical source.

Variable-control legend — used throughout this document:
  • HOLD CONSTANT Must not change within a session or across re-runs. Drift here invalidates comparisons. This is what you'll be tempted to fudge — don't.
  • MEASURE & LOG Allowed to vary but must be recorded per session (CSV metadata header or paper log). Without the value, the data is not analyzable.
  • FREE Can vary freely, no impact on comparability.
  • CRITICAL Sensitivity-critical control — if this drifts, the comparison breaks even if everything else is solid.

1 · Purpose (recap)

Stage 1 left the simulator-only classifier at 50% sensitivity / 44% FP on real bathroom CSVs. Closing that gap requires fitting each simulator component against real ground truth. This protocol specifies what to measure, in what order, and which signals.py parameter each measurement corrects.

2 · Hardware setup — what must be held constant

Item Setting Variable type Why it matters
MCU + firmware STM32F103C8T6 with ~/Documents/piezo_circuit/代码 - 调节发送频率/USER/main.c CRITICAL Different firmware → different output format / rate. Comparisons across sessions break.
INT_MARK 0 (mandatory, per Amendment 1 P1) CRITICAL Any other value violates the >= 1 kHz rate floor → CSV not admissible as Article I evidence.
Sensor MiniSense 100 (user-confirmed) HOLD CONSTANT Sensor swap → datasheet sensor model invalid. Requires Bill.

USB-serial adapter (CH340 / FTDI / CP2102 — converts UART ↔ USB CDC)
      │
      ▼ USB cable
Host laptop sees: /dev/ttyUSB0 (Linux) or COM3 (Windows) — a virtual serial port
```

UART is the *MCU-side* physical layer between the STM32 and the USB-serial chip. The operator capturing data on the laptop is reading a USB CDC virtual serial port, not raw UART. Calling it "UART capture" in operator-facing instructions is sloppy — the operator isn't touching UART, they're opening `/dev/ttyUSB0` with `screen` / `cat` / a Python script.

The metadata header I specified already gets this right (`transport: USART2_USB`), but section 5 / section 6 of the HTML still says "Start UART capture" etc. Inconsistent.

message.content: in the test, when we say tap, should we consider each tap are similar amount of force? so in this html and .md, could we have enough "repeatability" among each situations

content.text:
Good catch — and the honest answer is **no, the current protocol doesn't enforce enough repeatability**.

## The gap

| Measurement | Current "controls" | Real variability | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tap (A2-A4) | "fingernail tap, force = light/medium/hard log only" | **±50% peak amplitude** between human finger taps | The "envelope correlation ≥ 0.85" acceptance is amplitude-invariant (if we normalize), but force level shifts spectral content — a harder tap excites higher modes more, contaminating the FEA-fit. We end up fitting noise. |
| Walk (A5, B6) | "normal pace" | ±20% cadence, ±30% per-footfall force | Footstep-profile fit gets a smeared-out reference. |
| Drops (B1-B4) | "waist height (~1 m)" | ±50 mm release height variation, release-spin variation | Drop COR + multi-impact spacing extraction breaks if release angle / spin / height jitters. |
| Slump (B5) | "lowered slowly" | descent time varies ±2× | Two-stage signature shape varies with descent rate. |

## What I'd propose to fix it

| Measurement | Repeatability fix | Cost / effort |
|---|---|---|
| **Tap (A2-A4)** | **Build the calibrated drop jig.** 10 g steel ball (≈ a 6.4 mm dia ball bearing — $1) dropped through a vertical 100 mm tube (3D-print a tube with marked drop height + release plunger). Gives ±5% repeatability. **Use this instead of fingernail.** | 1 hour, one tube print |
| **Walk (A5, B6)** | Metronome app on phone at 100 BPM (= 1.67 steps/s). Operator paces to the metronome. | zero cost |
| **Drops (B1-B4)** | Simple PVC pipe / cardboard tube vertical guide. Release object from top, it falls straight. Removes spin + height jitter. | 30 min, $5 |
| **Slump (B5)** | Stopwatch + verbal "3-2-1-touch" countdown for descent timing. Target 2 s, accept ±0.5 s. | zero cost |

## And add per-measurement repeatability acceptance check

For each set of N repeats at one condition, compute the **coefficient of variation (CoV)** of the peak amplitude across repeats. Reject the set if it's above:

| Measurement | CoV threshold | If exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Tap with jig | < 10% | Re-check jig (ball seated? tube vertical?) |
| Tap with fingernail (fallback) | < 25% | Re-do the run; finger is too inconsistent that session |
| Drops with guide | < 15% | Re-check guide alignment |
| Walk | < 20% (per-footfall) | Operator went off-tempo; re-record with metronome |

## And bump N per cell

Currently 5 taps per distance, 5–15 events per drop condition. With ±50% variability, the standard error on the mean of 5 = 50%/√5 ≈ 22% — too noisy to fit anything tight. With the jig (±5%), 5 is plenty. With finger taps, you'd want 15+ to get the SEM down.

Proposed: keep N=5 if jig is built, bump to N=15 if relying on finger.

---

**My recommendation:** build the jig (it's an evening's work), keep N=5, add the CoV check. The whole repeatability problem becomes a non-issue.

Want me to update the .md and .html with these additions (calibrated-jig as recommended-not-optional, metronome for walks, drop guide, per-measurement CoV acceptance, conditional N-per-cell rule)?

message.content: what is a JIG?

content.text:
A **jig** = a simple custom-built fixture whose job is to make a manual operation repeatable. You build it once, then every use produces a near-identical result without the operator having to be careful.

For our "tap jig," it's literally a tube + ball + release mechanism:

```
            ┌──┐  ← thumb release at top (lift a pin or tilt to drop)
            │  │
            │  │ ← marked drop height: 100 mm
            │  │   (the ball starts from here every time)
            │● │
            │  │
            │  │
            │  │
        ┌───┴──┴───┐ ← tube base / standoff sits on the tile
        │          │
═══════════════════════════ ← tile surface (this is the "tap" point)
```

Components, total cost ~$3:
- **6.4 mm steel ball bearing** — gives consistent 10 g impact mass
- **Vertical tube** (3D-printed PLA, or a piece of acrylic / brass pipe) ~100 mm tall, just wider than the ball
- **Release mechanism** at the top — could be as simple as: cover the top with your thumb, lift thumb to release. More elegant: a small horizontal pin you pull out to drop the ball. Or a tilting cap.
- **Base** — flat ring or feet so the tube stands vertical on the tile

How it removes variability:
- Same ball every time → same mass
- Same drop height → same impact velocity (`v = √(2gh)` — physics, not operator skill)
- Same impact point → same coupling location
- Ball is small and rigid → impulse is short and clean (like an impact hammer)

Versus a fingernail tap: your finger force varies ±50% trial-to-trial because muscle output is noisy. The ball-in-tube has no human in the loop after "press release" — physics determines the impact.

You'd build a separate (bigger) one for the drop tests too — same idea, scaled up:

```
              ┌────┐
              │    │  ← marked release height (1 m for water-bottle test)
              │    │
              │ ▢  │  ← object sits here (bottle / phone / etc.)
              │    │
              │    │
        ┌─────┴────┴─────┐
        │      tube      │
═══════════════════════════ ← tile
```

For the drop tests, the "tube" can just be a piece of cardboard tubing or PVC pipe wide enough for the object to fall through without scraping. It doesn't need a release mechanism — just stand the tube vertical, lower the object to the marked height, let go.

TL;DR: **a jig is "the cardboard tube that makes you stop having to be careful."** Half an hour with whatever you have at home (PVC scrap, an old paper towel tube taped to a frame, a 3D-printed tube) replaces an entire failure mode.

message.content: okay, interesting, but have you considered the fact that the ground noise still exist?

content.text:
Excellent catch — the jig solves operator variability but **doesn't help with bathroom ambient noise**, and the noise floor changes a lot of what I said.

## What noise does to the tap test

The signal we record at distance *d* is:

```
measured(t) = tap_response(t, d) + noise(t)
```

The tap signal **decays with distance** (geometric spread + plate damping), but noise is roughly constant amplitude wherever the sensor sits. So:

| Distance | Tap peak (relative) | Noise floor | SNR | Practical impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 m | 1.0 (reference) | ~0.05 | ~26 dB | Noise barely matters |
| 1.5 m | ~0.3 | ~0.05 | ~16 dB | Noise visible in ringdown |
| 2.5 m | ~0.1 | ~0.05 | ~6 dB | **Noise dominates the late ringdown** — exactly the part we use to fit ζ_plate |

So even with a perfect jig (±5% impact force), the *measured* CoV at 2.5 m can be 30-50% because the noise variance dominates after the tap's transient. Your real per-tap force is identical; the noise on top of it isn't.

## What we can do about it — protocol additions

### 1. Coherent averaging across repeats

Instead of treating each tap as one independent observation, **align them on the impact onset and average them**. For N=5 aligned taps, independent noise drops by √5 ≈ 2.2×. For N=10, by √10 ≈ 3.2×.

This means: at 2.5 m, **bumping N from 5 to 10 buys you another 3 dB of effective SNR for free**, with the jig handling the alignment naturally (same release → same onset).

### 2. Pre-tap + post-tap noise window in each recording

Every tap CSV should contain:
- ~1 s of recording **before** the first tap
- ~1 s of recording **after** the last tap's ringdown

This characterizes the *current* noise floor at recording time (not just the global A1 baseline). It's the per-tap noise reference for subtraction or SNR computation.

### 3. Per-recording SNR acceptance check

Before accepting a tap-test recording, compute:

```
SNR = peak_amplitude / RMS(pre_tap_window)
```

| Distance | Required SNR | Action if fail |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 m | ≥ 20 dB | Re-check coupling (something compliant in the mount) |
| 1.5 m | ≥ 15 dB | Quiet the room further (vent off? wait for washer to stop?) |
| 2.5 m | ≥ 10 dB | Same + increase N to 15 |

### 4. Explicit "quiet conditions" enforcement during taps (not just baseline)

Currently the protocol says quiet for A1 (baseline) but doesn't enforce it for A2-A4 (taps). Should say:

> During A2-A4: vent OFF if it can be turned off, shower OFF, no flush during recording. If a neighbor washer is running, defer this session. The tap-test noise floor must match the A1 baseline conditions ± 3 dB or rerun.

### 5. Operator-presence noise: pick a stand position and stick to it

The operator's body adds ~0.01-0.05 g of micro-motion just by standing nearby. For 2.5 m taps, that's comparable to the noise floor.

Fix: **the operator stands at a marked spot during the tap recording**, and that spot is the same across all taps and across re-installs. Better: operator triggers the jig with a string pull from 2-3 m away (well behind the sensor, so any operator-induced floor motion arrives from a known direction).

### 6. Time-of-day repeatability check

The bathroom is not stationary — the vent cycles, neighbors flush, washer runs. To characterize this:
- Repeat A1 baseline once at recording start and once at recording end
- If baseline PSD shifts > 6 dB between the two, the noise was non-stationary during the session → flag the session and consider rerunning

## The deeper consequence

This also means the **acceptance residuals I wrote earlier are too optimistic**:

- "Per-tap envelope correlation ≥ 0.85" — that's achievable at 0.5 m, marginal at 1.5 m, *not* achievable at 2.5 m without coherent averaging
- "Ringdown τ within ±30%" — ringdown is the late-time, low-amplitude part = most contaminated by noise = hardest to fit

Should be split per distance:

| Distance | Envelope correlation target | Ringdown τ tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 m | ≥ 0.90 | ±20% |
| 1.5 m | ≥ 0.80 | ±30% |
| 2.5 m | ≥ 0.70 (or use coherently-averaged trace) | ±50% (or refit on averaged trace) |

## TL;DR

The jig kills operator variability. Noise still kills SNR at distance. Fixes:
1. **Pre/post-tap noise window** in every recording
2. **SNR acceptance check** (varies by distance)
3. **Coherent averaging** across N repeats (jig makes this trivial — onsets align)
4. **Quiet conditions** explicit for taps, not just baseline
5. **Operator stand position** marked and consistent (or remote-trigger via string)
6. **Time-of-day stationarity check** (baseline at session start AND end)
7. **Distance-dependent residual targets** instead of one-size-fits-all

This is a substantive enough change to the protocol that I'd want to update both the .md and .html — and probably add a new "Noise" section between sections 6 and 7. Want me to do that pass?

You're absolutely right — and the math backs you up. Let me run the actual numbers.

## Energy comparison

| Impulse source | Mass | Drop / impact | Kinetic energy at impact | Comparable to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original 10 g ball / 100 mm | 10 g | v = 1.4 m/s | **0.01 J** | Background micro-vibration |
| Walking footstep (one heel strike) | (70 kg person) | — | **~35 J** | What we want to detect |
| Catfood-bag drop (B4) | ~500 g / 1 m | v = 4.4 m/s | **~5 J** | A soft fall |
| Real human fall | 70 kg | partial | **~20+ J** | Worst case |

The 10 g ball is **~3500× quieter** than a footstep. At 2.5 m from the sensor, after geometric spread and plate damping, what reaches the sensor is buried in the noise floor. Useless for IR fitting at far distance.

## The fix: use a bigger calibrated impulse

Three options at increasing energy:

| Option | Setup | Energy | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Heavier ball** | 100 g steel ball, 200 mm drop in tube | ~0.2 J (~20× the 10g ball) | Still short contact (~0.1 ms) → broadband spectrum, still cheap, easy to build | Marginal SNR at 2.5 m |
| **Rubber-tip drop hammer** | 500 g hammer head with rubber tip, 200–500 mm drop via guided tube | ~1–2.5 J | Strong SNR everywhere. The rubber tip prevents tile damage. | Longer contact time (~10 ms) → narrower spectrum (mostly < 200 Hz). For fall detection, that band IS what we care about, so this is fine. |
| **Just use the catfood-bag drop itself** | The existing B4 catfood drop, treated as the calibrated impulse | ~5 J | **One less protocol step.** Same energy scale as the events we want to detect → IR fit is at the operating point that matters. Procedure already in the plan. | Even longer contact time, narrower spectrum (mostly < 100 Hz). Drop variability slightly higher than a ball-in-tube. |

## The real insight your question pointed at

**Why have a separate tap test at all if the catfood-bag drop is already a calibrated impulse at known mass and drop height?**

If we tighten the catfood-bag drop repeatability (a wide vertical drop tube guide, fixed release height marked with tape, weighed bag), the catfood drop **becomes** the IR characterization impulse — at the right energy level — and we just merge A2-A4 into B4.

Concretely the merged protocol would be:

- B4 already drops catfood at 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 10 each = **30 trials at 3 distances**, more than enough for averaging
- The catfood is heavy enough that even at 2.5 m the signal is well above noise
- The drop energy (~5 J) is in the same regime as what the device will see in deployment — so we're fitting the IR at the operating point, not extrapolating from a tiny ball-tap up to a fall

You'd lose the high-frequency (>100 Hz) part of the plate response, but **the simulator's band of interest is 5–200 Hz anyway**, and the floor-plate FEA's modes that matter for fall detection all sit below 100 Hz. The high-frequency stuff is dominated by the sensor's own 75 Hz resonance and damping, which is from the datasheet — we don't need to fit it from data.

## Recommendation

Drop the separate tap test (A2-A4). Replace with:

- **A-phase tap test → just the per-session sanity check** (1 finger tap, no jig needed, qualitative pass/fail)
- **B4 catfood-bag drop becomes the IR characterization data** — with a vertical drop-guide tube so the drop is highly repeatable
- **The IR fit and the fall-trajectory fit both use the same B4 dataset**

Net effect: protocol gets simpler (one fewer phase), data quality goes up (right energy scale, better SNR everywhere), and one fewer custom jig to build.

Want me to update the .md and .html with this restructuring? It's a fairly significant change — merging A2-A4 into B4 — so worth confirming before I do the pass.

content.text:
Walkthrough for the official Notion MCP server. ~5 minutes start to finish.

## Step 1 — Create the Notion integration (in Notion)

1. Go to https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations
2. Click **"+ New integration"**
3. Name it something like "Claude Code"
4. Associate it with your workspace
5. Type: **Internal**
6. Capabilities: leave defaults (Read content, Update content, Insert content)
7. Click **Save**
8. Copy the **Internal Integration Secret** (starts with `secret_…` or `ntn_…`)

## Step 2 — Share your Notion pages with the integration

Notion integrations don't see anything until you explicitly share pages with them.

- Open the Notion page (or parent page / database) you want me to read/write
- Click **"…"** (top right) → **Connections** → **Connect to** → pick "Claude Code"
- Share at the highest level you're comfortable with; child pages inherit

If you want me to write the data-collection protocol into a specific page, share that page (or its parent).

## Step 3 — Add the MCP server to Claude Code

Run this in your shell (replace `<TOKEN>` with the integration secret from step 1):

```bash
claude mcp add notion -s user \
  -e NOTION_API_KEY=<TOKEN> \
  -- npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server
```

What this does:
- `-s user` = available across all your Claude Code projects
- `-e NOTION_API_KEY=…` = passes the integration token as an env var
- `npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server` = runs the official Notion MCP via npx (no global install needed; npx fetches it on first run)

## Step 4 — Restart this Claude Code session

The MCP server only loads at session start. After you've run the `claude mcp add` command, exit this session (Ctrl+C twice or `/quit`) and start a new one. The Notion tools should then appear in my toolset.

## Step 5 — Test it

Once restarted, you can verify by:
- Run `/mcp` — should list `notion` as connected
- Or just ask me to "search my Notion for pages about piezo_fall" — I'll use the MCP to query

---

**A few practical notes:**

- The token is stored in your local Claude config (`~/.claude.json`). Don't commit that file.
- If you ever want to revoke access, delete the integration in Notion settings — it kills the token instantly.
- The official MCP supports: search, page read, page create, block append/update/delete, database query, comment read/write.
- If `npx` is slow on first run, you can install the package globally instead: `npm install -g @notionhq/notion-mcp-server` and then change `npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server` to just `notion-mcp-server` in the `claude mcp add` command.

Let me know once you've run step 3 and restarted — I'll then have direct read/write access and can push the data collection protocol straight into your Notion. Or if any step trips up, drop the error message here and I'll debug.

properties.title: piezo_fall — Real-to-Sim Correction Data Collection Protocol

pages.content:
Source: `docs/data_collection_protocol.md` in `crucible_lite/piezo_fall` (commit b911e0f, 2026-05-16). Markdown is canonical. This Notion page is a reading rendition with variable-control highlights. ## Variable-control legend Used throughout this document — same tags on every section so you can scan quickly. - **CRITICAL** Sensitivity-critical control. If this drifts, the comparison breaks even if everything else is solid. Single most likely failure source. - **HOLD CONSTANT** Must not change within a session or across re-runs. Drift here invalidates comparisons. - **MEASURE & LOG** Allowed to vary but must be recorded (CSV metadata or paper log). Without the value, the data is not analyzable. - **FREE** Can vary freely, no impact on comparability. ## 1 · Purpose Stage 1 left the simulator-only classifier at **50% sensitivity / 44% FP** on real bathroom CSVs. Closing that gap requires fitting each simulator component against real ground truth. This protocol specifies what to measure, in what order, and which `signals.py` parameter each measurement corrects. The tap test is one piece (the IR-fitting piece); the full plan covers tap + walk + drop + fall-surrogate + noise so a single bathroom deployment captures everything needed. ## 2 · Hardware setup — what must be held constant
**Item** **Setting** **Variable type** **Why it matters**
MCU + firmware STM32F103C8T6 with `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/代码 - 调节发送频率/USER/main.c` CRITICAL Different firmware → different output format / rate. Comparisons across sessions break.
`INT_MARK` **0** (mandatory, per Amendment 1 P1) CRITICAL Any other value violates the ≥1 kHz rate floor → CSV not admissible as Article I evidence.
Sensor MiniSense 100 (user-confirmed) HOLD CONSTANT Sensor swap → datasheet sensor model invalid. Requires Bill.
Housing `ground_cantilever_housing.stp`, PLA, 100% infill HOLD CONSTANT Re-printing with different infill or material shifts the follow-the-floor resonance.
Preload weight **~200 g** (range 100–500 g acceptable; pick one and stay) HOLD CONSTANT within a study Different preload → different rocking margin and follow-the-floor resonance.
Transport USART2 (PA2/PA3) → USB-serial @ 115200 baud, FireWater `%.3f\n` CRITICAL Different transport → different buffering → different effective sample rate / drops.
Measured rate Whatever it actually is — typical ~1.38 kHz on USART2-USB MEASURE & LOG Must be in CSV header per Case 1 ruling. **Compute**, don't assume.
Bathroom / tile / device xy Whatever the actual install is MEASURE & LOG Different bathrooms produce different IRs — that's the point of multi-bathroom planning.
## 3 · Sample-rate gate (run before every session) **Gate check (10 s):** capture 10 s of USART2 output, compute `measured_rate_hz = lines / wall_clock_elapsed`. **Must be ≥ 1000 Hz.** If less: abort. INT_MARK is wrong, transport is buffering, or the firmware build is the wrong one. Per Case 1, recordings below 1 kHz are *not admissible* as Article I evidence. ## 4 · Mandatory CSV metadata header (per Case 1) ``` # int_mark: 0 CRITICAL # transport: USART2_USB HOLD # measured_rate_hz: 1380 MEASURE # bathroom_id: bathroom_A MEASURE # tile_size_mm: 200x200 MEASURE # device_xy_in_room: "0.3m W wall, 0.5m S wall" MEASURE # preload_mass_g: 200 HOLD # operator: shiyao MEASURE # date: 2026-05-XX MEASURE # session_id: 001 MEASURE # measurement_type: tap_0.5m MEASURE ``` Missing fields → CSV not admissible. Don't proceed without them. ## 5 · Per-session mount sanity check (~1 min) 1. Place housing on tile. Confirm baseplate is flush — no rocking when pushing the cap with a finger. 2. Place 200 g weight on top platform. 3. Start USART2 capture. 4. Tap tile 30 cm from housing with a fingernail. **5 taps, ~2 s apart.** 5. Stop capture, inspect: - **Pass:** clean impulse, ringdown < 50 ms, no inter-tap oscillation - **Fail:** ringdown > 200 ms (compliant contact), delayed rise (foam), large oscillation between taps (loose preload / rocking baseplate) If fail: alcohol-wipe the tile, re-seat the housing, repeat. **Do not proceed to data collection until sanity check passes.** Bad coupling silently contaminates everything downstream. ## 6 · The protocol as one table (per bathroom) Each row is a discrete measurement. The two highlighted columns are the experimental controls — what must be held constant vs measured/logged for that specific measurement.
**#** **Phase** **Duration** **Measurement & output file** **What must be HELD CONSTANT** **What must be MEASURED & LOGGED** **Fixes in `signals.py`** **Acceptance residual**
0Sanity1 min Tap 30 cm × 5 (verify, not saved) tap source (fingernail), tap location (30 cm), preload (200 g) pass/fail observation in operator log n/a — verifies mount only ringdown < 50 ms, no inter-tap oscillation
A1Install calib60 s Quiet baseline, no one in room → `_baseline.csv` no one in room, appliances OFF except vent (if normally on), door state — pick one and stay vent state, door state, time of day `bg_environmental_noise` per-peak amplitudes Real PSD vs sim PSD ±6 dB, 1–500 Hz
A2Install calib5 taps Tap at 0.5 m → `_tap_0.5m.csv` CRITICAL tap source (jig or same finger), tap location (marked with tape!), 5 taps ≥ 2 s apart, no other movement in room tap location xy in room, tap force (light/medium/hard) Floor-plate FEA ζ, modal density, near-field gain Per-tap envelope correlation ≥ 0.85
A3Install calib5 taps Tap at 1.5 m → `_tap_1.5m.csv` CRITICAL same tap source as A2, location marked with tape, 5 taps ≥ 2 s apart tap location xy, tap force level Same + `REAL_TO_SIM_SCALE` (spatial decay) Ringdown τ ±30%
A4Install calib5 taps Tap at 2.5 m → `_tap_2.5m.csv` CRITICAL same as A2/A3 tap location xy, tap force level Same + far-field decay Same
A5Install calib60 s Calibration walk → `_walk.csv` one operator, normal pace (~2 steps/s), footwear (barefoot / socks / sole) — pick one and stay for the whole study operator weight (kg), footwear, rough path description `_footstep_force_profile` peak, contact time Peak mean ±20%, cadence KS p > 0.05
B1Events~5 min Water bottle drops × 15 (0.5/1.5/2.5 m × 5) → `_drop_water.csv` CRITICAL drop height (waist ~1 m, measure once with a stick and keep it), same bottle (mass + fill level), orientation at release (cap up) bottle mass (g with current fill), drop height (m), drop location xy `drop_trajectory` rigid `rebound_pattern` (COR, multi-impact spacing) Multi-peak count ±1, decay corr ≥ 0.80
B2Events~3 min Phone drops × 10 → `_drop_phone.csv` same phone, same drop height as B1, same orientation (screen up) phone mass (g), drop height, drop location xy Same, lower-mass rigid Same
B3Events~3 min Glass drops × 10 → `_drop_glass.csv` same glass type each time (or label per glass), same drop height, drop into contained area glass mass (g), drop height, drop location xy, did it break? (yes/no) `drop_trajectory` `shatter` pattern (multi-impact) Same
B4Events~10 min Catfood-bag drops × 30 (0.5/1.5/2.5 m × 10; 5 of the 1.5m with body-in-path) → `_fall_catfood.csv` CRITICAL same catfood bag (mass + fill), drop height (waist), body-in-path means operator stands DIRECTLY between drop point and sensor bag mass (g), drop height, drop xy, body-in-path? yes/no, operator weight `fall_trajectory` peak + `body_absorption_db` (currently 5 dB guess) Body-in-vs-out amplitude ratio ±2 dB
B5Events~5 min Slow-slump surrogate × 10 → `_fall_slump.csv` same heavy bag (~10 kg), lowered slowly by hand to floor (not dropped) — target descent time (e.g. 2 s) and try to match it bag mass, descent time (s), descent location xy `fall_slump` two-stage profile (rumble onset + impact) Visual match in plot review
B6Events5 min Extra walking → `_walk_extra.csv` same operator + footwear as A5 vary the paces deliberately (slow / normal / fast) and log time-windows of each Walking cadence statistics (augments A5) Cadence distribution coverage
B7Noise60 s Shower running → `_noise_shower.csv` water on full, no operator movement, door state same as A1 flow rate setting (low/med/high), water temperature (hot/cold) if relevant `noise_shower` PSD amplitudes Per-source PSD ±6 dB
B8Noise60 s Vent on → `_noise_vent.csv` vent on at full speed, no other source vent fan rating (W or m³/h) if known `noise_vent` PSD amplitudes Same
B9Noise5 flushes Toilet flush × 5 → `_noise_flush.csv` same toilet, wait for refill between flushes, ~30 s gap flush-to-flush gap (s), tank refill duration (s) `noise_flush` transient amplitude + duration Same
B10Noise60 s + spin-up Washer (if applicable) → `_noise_washer.csv` washer cycle stage (agitate vs spin), load size repeatable across studies cycle stage, load type, distance from bathroom (m) `noise_washer_local` / `_neighbor` PSD Same
—Logcontinuous Handwritten / phone-notes labels → `_log.md` log format (timestamp + class + distance + body-in-path + anomaly per line) everything n/a — labeling n/a
**Total per-bathroom time:** ~50–60 min active + 5 min calibration. One session, one device deploy, one operator. ## 7 · Variables that matter most — don't change mid-study **If you change any of these between A-phase and B-phase, or between sessions in the same bathroom, your data is not comparable. Pick once and stick:** - CRITICAL `INT_MARK` value (must stay 0) - CRITICAL tap source (fingernail vs jig — pick one and stick across A2/A3/A4) - CRITICAL tap locations (marked with tape, kept across re-installs) - CRITICAL operator footwear (barefoot / socks / sole) across A5 + B6 - CRITICAL drop height across B1/B2/B3/B4 - CRITICAL "body in path" means operator *directly* between drop and sensor — not off-axis - HOLD preload weight (~200 g, no swap mid-study) - HOLD housing (don't re-print between sessions) - HOLD sensor (no swap) - HOLD door state during baseline + noise recordings - HOLD bathroom appliance state during baseline (everything OFF except what's normally on) **Measure & log (allowed to vary):** - `measured_rate_hz` per session - bag / bottle / phone / glass mass - operator weight (kg) - tile size + device xy in room - drop locations xy - per-event anomalies (bounced off wall, wet floor, etc.) **Free to vary, no impact:** - time of day (within reason — avoid 3 AM dead silence vs 9 AM neighbor noise extremes) - ambient temperature (within room range) - humidity (within bathroom-normal range) ## 8 · After data — the correction loop
**Step** **Who** **What** **Output**
1Operator Run section 6 on bathroom A `data/bathroom_A/*.csv`
2Claude Draft fit scripts (`fit_floor_ir.py`, `fit_footstep.py`, `fit_drop_rebound.py`, `fit_body_absorption.py`, `fit_confuser_noise.py`) and a single Bill: *Sim-to-real v3 corrections from bathroom_A* Bill draft + fit scripts
3Judicial hearing Debate the Bill Case ruling
4Claude If passed: apply fits to `signals.py`, retrain classifier, rerun sim-to-real v3 Updated `signals.py`, `algorithm.py`, `scripts/sim_to_real_test_v3.py` output
5Decision gate Inspect v3 vs trigger criteria below "Stay at 1 bathroom" or "Expand to 3"
## 9 · The expand-to-3 trigger (pre-committed)
**v3 result on bathroom A** **Decision** **Why**
Sens ≥ 80%, FP ≤ 10% **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Correction worked here, but need to prove not just over-fit to one tile
Sens 60–80% or FP 10–25% **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Structure looks OK but needs more data
Sens < 60% or FP > 25% **Stay at 1, draft simulator-structure Bills** Extra data won't fix a wrong-shaped simulator; revisit modeling assumptions (e.g. multi-tile mosaic, FEA mode selection)
Tap-test repeatability (A2–A4) corr < 0.7 across the 5 repeats **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Mount / tile coupling unstable — need to see if it's bathroom A or general
## 10 · Open questions before first execution 1. **Tap source standardization.** Fingernail tap is operator-dependent (±50%). Build a jig: 10 g steel ball dropped through a 100 mm vertical tube. Removes operator entirely. Note: **also pending discussion** — the small ball may have insufficient SNR vs ambient noise at 2.5 m; consider larger calibrated drop (100 g ball / 200 mm), or use the catfood-bag drop itself as the calibrated IR-fitting impulse. 2. **Sample-rate metadata.** Recommend inline: record session wall-clock start + CSV row count, derive rate post-hoc. 3. **Storage path.** `data/` symlinked outside repo with `.gitignore` to avoid bloating git with large CSVs. 4. **Legacy CSV admission.** Existing `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/bathroom_testing/{catfood,water,step}_201505.csv` should be migrated under `data/bathroom_legacy/` with metadata headers retro-fitted (operator-attested, not measured). Flag the asymmetry in any v3 report. 5. **Event segmentation tool.** Phase B produces 30-minute CSVs with discrete events. Need a tool (script or simple GUI) to extract event windows from log timestamps. Build alongside Phase B execution. --- **Canonical source:** `docs/data_collection_protocol.md` in the `crucible_lite` repo, branch `piezo_fall`. See also `docs/data_collection_protocol.html` for a styled standalone reading rendition.

---
name: feedback-tap-vs-impulse
description: Terminology rule for piezo_fall — "tap" only for qualitative checks; use "impulse" when the measurement produces a number we compare quantitatively.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When writing protocols, docs, or code for piezo_fall (and similar mechanical-impulse work), use the word "tap" ONLY for qualitative observations where the result is a go/no-go (e.g. "fingernail tap on the tile to check if the mount rings"). When the impulse is calibrated and the result is a number used for comparison across trials, distances, bathrooms, or fitting (e.g. impulse response for floor-plate FEA fitting), use "impulse" or "impulse test" instead.

**Why:** the word "tap" carries connotations of manual / hand-driven / variable magnitude / informal. Using it for a measurement that gets *fit against quantitatively* sets the wrong expectation and invites operator-variability sloppiness. The engineering-precise term is "impulse" (broadband mechanical input for IR characterization). Modal testing labs use "impulse hammer test" / "drop weight test" for the same reason.

**How to apply:**
- "tap test" (the quantitative IR-fitting measurement) → "impulse test"
- File names like `tap_0.5m.csv` → `impulse_0.5m.csv`
- "tap source" → "impulse source"
- KEEP "fingernail tap" / "tap sanity check" for the qualitative per-session mount-OK verification
- KEEP "tap" in casual descriptions where the input genuinely is a finger tap and the output is just visual pass/fail

content.subject: Hearing for Bill 001 — Amendment 1 sample-rate revision
content.description: Bill 001 enacted with modification — Case 1 ruling: A1 P1 rate floor raised to ≥1.5 kHz (mechanically enforces INT_MARK=0), + mandatory CSV metadata (int_mark, transport, measured_rate_hz). Commit 4bb237c.

content.subject: Confirm deployed sensor = MiniSense 100 (BOM or part marking vs datasheet)
content.description: RESOLVED 2026-05-16. Deployed sensor is NOT a MiniSense 100. Evidence: (1) ~/Documents/piezo_circuit/SENSOR_MOUNTING.md describes a custom-assembled cantilever — 25mm×8mm×28µm bare PVDF strip + 2-10g brass/steel proof mass, base epoxied to floor, resonance 50-500 Hz depending on geometry; (2) BOM lists only conditioning electronics (CA3140/MAX44248 + 100 MΩ bias R48), no commercial sensor module; (3) zero "MiniSense" hits in original repo. The MiniSense 100 assumption originated in our simulator work, not the hardware record. Simulator sensor model fn/ζ/sensitivity require revision via Bill once the actual cantilever is tap-tested.

content.subject: Plan real-to-sim correction data collection (taps + walks + drops + falls)
content.description: Drafted in docs/data_collection_protocol.md (2026-05-16). Single coherent plan covering full real-to-sim correction dataset, not just tap test. Scope: 1 bathroom first with explicit expand-to-3 trigger criteria. Each measurement explicitly tied to a simulator component it fits + acceptance residual. After data collected, fit scripts + simulator updates go through a single Bill ("Sim-to-real v3 corrections").

content.subject: Sim-to-real v2 with corrected tag mapping + distance grouping
content.description: Tag mapping: step→confuser_step, fall→fall_fast (catfood=body fall surrogate), other→confuser_drop_phone (water=rigid drop). Per-distance grouping via peak-sorted. Catfood 1.5m split into unblocked (top 3) and blocked (bottom 3) per drop-human-sensor experimental design. Body-absorption (5 dB) added to fall_trajectory.

content.text:
Yes — and that's the logical consequence of the rename. If the result is a number we're going to compare quantitatively, the source has to be calibrated (jig), not a fingernail. The rename forces the question: making me realize that the "fingernail vs jig — operator chooses" wording I had was wrong. For Phase A2-A4 (the impulse test) the jig is required, not optional. Fingernail stays only for Phase 0 sanity check, which is genuinely qualitative.

Doing both edits together — tap → impulse for quantitative, AND elevating the jig from "optional refinement" to required.

# Stage 1 Baseline — Final Sim-to-Real Result (2026-05-16)

This document records the Stage 1 simulator + classifier performance baseline
at the end of the simulator-only iteration phase. Stage 1 is HELD HERE pending
real data collection (see `docs/data_collection_protocol.md` when written).

---

## TL;DR

The simulator + RandomForest classifier — trained ONLY on synthetic data — achieves
on real bathroom CSVs (30 events across step / catfood-fall / water-drop classes,
distance-resolved at 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.0 m):

| Metric | Value | Target | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sensitivity (catfood fall surrogates → fall) | **6/12 = 50.0%** | ≥ 95% | FAILS |
| FP rate (steps + water bottle drops → fall) | **8/18 = 44.4%** | ≤ 1/week | FAILS |

This is the honest simulator-only ceiling. Any further improvement requires
real training data, not simulator tweaks.

---

## Per-distance per-class breakdown

| Source | Tag | Real meaning | Distance | n | Result | Correct % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| step_201505 | step | walking (NOT-fall) | 0.5 m | 3 | 2/3 wrongly fall | 33% |
| step_201505 | step | walking | 1.5 m | 3 | 1/3 wrongly fall | 67% |
| step_201505 | step | walking | 2.0 m | 3 | 1/3 wrongly fall | 67% |
| water_201505 | other | water-bottle drop (NOT-fall, rigid object confuser) | 0.5 m | 3 | 2/3 wrongly fall | 33% |
| water_201505 | other | water-bottle drop | 1.5 m | 3 | 1/3 wrongly fall | 67% |
| water_201505 | other | water-bottle drop | 2.0 m | 3 | 1/3 wrongly fall | 67% |
| catfood_201505 | fall | body-fall surrogate (catfood bag) | 0.5 m | 3 | 2/3 caught | 67% |
| catfood_201505 | fall | body-fall surrogate | 1.5m_unblocked (human at far side) | 3 | 1/3 caught | 33% |
| catfood_201505 | fall | body-fall surrogate | 1.5m_blocked (human between) | 3 | 1/3 caught | 33% |
| catfood_201505 | fall | body-fall surrogate | 2.0 m | 3 | 2/3 caught | 67% |

## Key observation: amplitude bias

The detector is biased to call CLOSE/HIGH-AMPLITUDE signals "fall" regardless of
class. Close events of any class get flagged ~67% of the time; far events get
flagged ~33% of the time. The new scale-invariant features
(post_pre_rms_ratio, low/high band fractions) helped on synthetic data but
don't dominate on real data with realistic noise + amplitude variation.

## Body absorption test (5 dB body-in-path attenuation)

The catfood 1.5m group had 6 events split into two experimental conditions:
3 "unblocked" (human at the far side from sensor — clear propagation path)
and 3 "blocked" (human between drop point and sensor — body absorbs signal).

Both groups caught at the same rate (1/3 = 33%). With only 3 events per
condition, the noise on this number is too high to validate or reject the
5 dB body-absorption hypothesis (which is implemented in `fall_trajectory`
as `body_absorption_db=5.0` default). Needs ≥ 10 events per condition.

## What this baseline tells us about simulator iteration

The previous validation result was misinterpreted due to wrong tag-to-class
mapping (commit a201022, 2026-05-15). After user clarifications and a
corrected sim-to-real script (`scripts/sim_to_real_test_v2.py`):

- The simulator + sensor + noise pipeline produces reasonable signals
- The classifier trained on synthetic data has an **amplitude bias** that
  doesn't reflect what real falls look like
- Simulator improvements (multi-impact rebound, body absorption,
  cantilever sensor model) reduced the misinterpretation gap but did
  NOT close the actual classifier shortcoming
- The remaining gap requires real training data; further simulator
  tuning yields diminishing returns

---

## State of the simulator at this baseline

`src/signals.py` (v3, commit 893b865 + later) implements:

| Stage | Component | Evidence type |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Backgrounds | vent (60/120/180 Hz tones), shower (broadband), washer (narrow-band), flush (transient) | LITERATURE + HAND-TUNED amplitudes |
| 2. Events | floor_sim FEA plate model (Kirchhoff, 25 modes, 2 geometries) for impacts; analytical slump | PHYSICS + LITERATURE force ranges (Cavanagh & Lafortune, Robinovitch) |
| 2'. Drop rebound | rigid / bouncy / soft_pkg / shatter patterns | LITERATURE (coefficient of restitution) |
| 2''. Body absorption | 5 dB attenuation on fall_trajectory impacts | EMPIRICAL (catfood drop-human-sensor data, n=3, weak validation) |
| 3. Sensor model | MiniSense 100 cantilever (75 Hz, ζ=0.092) + bias HP (6.5 Hz) | DATASHEET-VERIFIED |
| 4. Noise floor | Real bathroom spectrum (1/f + white + peaks at 25/60/91/120/183 Hz) | EMPIRICAL from bathroom_testing/step_201505.csv |

## State of the classifier

`src/algorithm.py` (commit bda4652 + later) — RandomForest with 13 features:
- 6 per-event physical: peak_amp, total_energy, duration_above_noise_ms,
  spectral_centroid_hz, decay_tau_ms, multi_peak_count
- 5 scale-invariant (added 2026-05-16): pre_event_rms, post_event_rms,
  post_pre_rms_ratio, low_band_energy_frac, high_band_energy_frac
- 2 temporal context: events_in_last_5s, time_since_last_event_s

Trained on 20 seeds × 13 profiles × 2 geometries (small + medium bathroom) =
~1067 events. Tested in v1 on 100 synthetic seeds × 13 profiles × 2 geometries
(89.6% sens, 4.1% FP on synthetic). Tested in v2 on 30 real events across 3
CSVs (50% sens, 44% FP — this baseline).

## 14-profile catalog

| Class | Profile | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| noise (5) | noise_vent, noise_shower, noise_flush, noise_washer_local, noise_washer_neighbor | continuous backgrounds, no events |
| confuser (5) | confuser_step, confuser_drop_phone, confuser_drop_heavy, confuser_drop_glass, walk_in_out | events that aren't falls |
| fall (4) | fall_fast, fall_slump, fall_after_walk, fall_softbody_surrogate | fall events (with -5 dB body absorption) |

## Open simulator gaps (will only be closed with real data)

1. **Amplitude bias in classifier** — features need redesign or real data to overcome
2. **Body-absorption value (5 dB) is a guess** — needs ≥ 10 events per condition to validate
3. **Multi-tile mosaic floor not modeled** — defer to install-time calibration (per generalization strategy in `docs/device_context.md`)
4. **Sensor identity assumption unverified** — task #31 (user visual inspection)
5. **Plate damping / geometry** — defer to install-time calibration (tap test)
6. **Real fall human data unavailable** — surrogates only (catfood bag is closest)

## What needs to happen before Stage 2

Per `docs/device_context.md` Install-Time Calibration Design section:

1. Collect real bathroom recordings with metadata per Case 1 ruling (int_mark,
   transport, measured_rate_hz) from multiple bathrooms (≥ 3 recommended)
2. Add real events to training data alongside synthetic
3. Build install-time calibration scripts (tap test + baseline + walk)
4. Verify deployed sensor identity (task #31)
5. Verify firmware streaming rate (Bill 002 ratified ≥ 1 kHz; INT_MARK=0
   required in deployment)

---

## Files and commits at baseline

- `src/signals.py` — simulator (FEA + sensor + noise + 14 profiles)
- `src/algorithm.py` — RandomForest classifier (13 features)
- `scripts/sim_to_real_test_v2.py` — corrected sim-to-real test
- `docs/governance/amendments.md` — A1 P1 at ≥ 1 kHz (Case 1+2)
- `docs/governance/case_law.md` — Case 1 (Bill 001) + Case 2 (Bill 002)
- `docs/governance/bills/` — Bill 001 (enacted, modified) + Bill 002 (enacted)
- `docs/plots/sim_layout_diagram.png` — sensor + event-zone visualization
- `docs/plots/sensor_model_bode.png` — sensor TF vs datasheet verification
- `docs/plots/real_noise_spectrum.png` — empirical noise basis
- `docs/plots/sim_render/` — 26 per-profile signal renderings
- `docs/plots/real_vs_synth_footstep*.png` — earlier sim-vs-real comparisons

Stage 1 is HELD at this baseline. Resume at Stage 2 only after real data is
collected and added to the training corpus.

---

## Post-baseline finding (2026-05-16): deployed sensor identity confirmed

Task #31 (originally "verify deployed sensor visual inspection", reframed to
"confirm part = MiniSense 100 via BOM/marking") resolved:
**user confirms the deployed sensor is a MiniSense 100**.

Context for future agents who read the source repo and get confused:
the original `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/` repo contains a general-purpose
PVDF front-end designed to work with any PVDF sensor (custom cantilever or
commercial). Its `SENSOR_MOUNTING.md` covers all three configurations
(bare PVDF film, custom PVDF + proof mass cantilever, PZT disc). Its BOM
lists only the conditioning electronics (CA3140 / MAX44248 front-end,
100 MΩ bias resistor R48), not the sensor itself, because the sensor is
modular. None of this contradicts the MiniSense 100 deployment for
piezo_fall — the front-end happens to be compatible with the MiniSense's
output impedance and bias requirement.

### Implications

- Simulator's cantilever model (fn=75 Hz, ζ=0.092, 1.1 V/g baseline,
  6 V/g at resonance, 6.5 Hz HP via 100 MΩ × ~250 pF) remains
  **datasheet-correct** and is the right reference for sim work.
- Action item: add an explicit "Sensor: MiniSense 100 (Measurement
  Specialties)" line to the BOM in `docs/device_context.md` so this
  doesn't have to be re-derived next session.
