content.text:
All docs + Notion updated and pushed (027ddc0). Now — designing the jig.

## Design goals

| Goal | Target | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Reproducible energy | CoV < 5% across drops | The whole point — replaces ±50% finger variability |
| SNR ≥ 15 dB at 2.5 m | ~0.1–1 J impact energy | Detectable above bathroom ambient noise floor |
| Short contact time | < 1 ms | Broadband spectrum → excites all modes for IR fitting |
| Same impact location every drop | ±2 mm | Spatial decay fitting needs known geometry |
| Operator hand far from impact | string-pull / pin-pull release | Operator body motion doesn't contaminate signal |
| Cheap to build | < $20 | Single-bathroom prototype; can iterate later |
| Doesn't damage tile | smooth steel on porcelain | Hard ceramic tolerates 0.2 J impact without marking |

## Recommended design — vertical drop-tube jig

```
                ╔═══════════════╗
                ║   pull-pin    ║ ← 1 mm steel rod through tube
                ╠══╪═════════╪══╣   (drilled hole each side)
                ║  ╪ ●━━━━━━ ╪  ║ ← steel ball rests on pin (loaded)
                ║  └─────────┘  ║
                ║               ║
                ║               ║
                ║   drop zone   ║ ← 300 mm drop height (marked)
                ║   PLA tube    ║
                ║   ID ~28 mm   ║
                ║   wall 3 mm   ║
                ║               ║
                ║               ║
                ╚═══════════════╝
              ╔═══════════════════╗
              ║   base plate      ║ ← 60 mm dia PLA disc, 4 mm thick
              ║   (open center)   ║   (tube glued vertical, hole below)
              ╚════╤═════════╤════╝
                   ▼         ▼
   ════════════════════════════════ ← tile surface
                   ↑
         Impact zone (ball falls clean
         through open bottom onto tile)
```

## Components (~$15 total)

| Part | Spec | Source | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Steel ball | 1″ (25.4 mm) chrome steel ball bearing, ~66 g | Amazon / McMaster #96455K56 | ~$2 |
| Tube + base | 3D-printed PLA: 350 mm tall × 34 mm OD × 28 mm ID, integrated 60 mm dia base plate with central hole | Your printer, ~25 g filament | ~$1 |
| Pull pin | 1 mm dia × 50 mm steel rod (paperclip works), with a small loop bent on one end | Hardware store / paperclip | ~$0 |
| String (optional) | Thin cord (fishing line, dental floss) tied to the pin loop | Anything | ~$0 |
| Bubble level (optional) | Tiny stick-on bullseye level | Hardware store | ~$3 |

**Print settings for the tube:** 4 walls, 100% infill on the base, 30% gyroid in the tube walls (full strength only needed at base). Inner surface should be smooth — print tube with seam to the back, fine layer height (0.15 mm), enable iron-top-layer if your printer supports it. A rough inner surface adds friction → variable drop time.

## Operating procedure

1. **Position:** place jig base on marked tile spot, tube vertical (check bubble level if you printed one in)
2. **Load:** insert pull-pin horizontally through the holes at the 300 mm mark
3. **Drop ball into tube** from top — ball settles onto pin
4. **Wait 2 s** for any rattle to damp
5. **Pull pin** (smoothly, sideways, with finger or string from 1 m away)
6. Ball falls 300 mm, exits open bottom of tube, hits tile
7. **Wait 2 s before next drop** (lets floor ringdown decay below noise floor)
8. **Retrieve ball** — it bounces a little; either let it settle, pick it up, reload

If using string release: pull from behind the sensor (2+ m away from the jig), so any operator-induced floor motion arrives at the sensor *before* the ball's impulse and is excluded by onset-aligned averaging.

## Energy calculations for this design

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Ball mass | 0.066 kg |
| Drop height | 0.30 m |
| Impact velocity v = √(2gh) | 2.43 m/s |
| Kinetic energy | **0.195 J** (~20× the original 10 g/100 mm proposal) |
| Momentum | 0.16 kg·m/s |
| Estimated contact time | ~50–100 μs (steel-on-porcelain Hertz contact) |
| Spectral content extends to | ~5 kHz (well past anything we care about) |
| Estimated signal at sensor | ~0.05–0.5 g at 0.5 m, ~0.01–0.05 g at 2.5 m (highly tile-dependent) |

## Validation — how to confirm the jig is working

Before trusting any data from it, run a **jig-only repeatability test**:

1. Place jig at 1.0 m from sensor (single fixed distance)
2. Drop 10 times in sequence with 2 s between
3. Compute peak amplitude of each drop's recorded impulse
4. Compute CoV (std / mean) of those 10 peaks

| Result | Verdict |
|---|---|
| CoV < 5% | Jig is well-controlled. Proceed with A2/A3/A4. |
| 5% ≤ CoV < 10% | Acceptable but check: tube vertical? ball clean? pin pulled smoothly? |
| 10% ≤ CoV < 20% | Investigate: ball getting stuck on tube wall? Pin not quite at the same depth each load? Operator's pull is jerky? |
| CoV ≥ 20% | Don't use — debug first |

## If SNR is still bad at 2.5 m (escalation path)

If even with the jig, 2.5 m drops don't give SNR ≥ 10 dB:

| Escalation | Change | New energy |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Increase drop height to 500 mm | ~0.32 J (1.6×) |
| 2 | Use 100 g ball (1.25″, ~130 g actual) at 500 mm | ~0.65 J (3.3×) |
| 3 | Use 200 g ball (1.5″, ~225 g actual) at 500 mm | ~1.1 J (5.6×) |
| 4 | **Skip the dedicated jig.** Use the catfood-bag drop (Phase B4) directly as the calibrated impulse for IR fitting. ~5 J, well above noise at any reasonable distance. | ~5 J |

Each step is one print-change away (longer tube, bigger ball). Don't pre-build all four — build option 1 (300 mm, 66 g ball), test, escalate only if needed.

## Want this as a separate doc + Notion page?

I can write this up as `docs/impulse_jig_design.md` in the repo and add a Jig Design subpage under the protocol's Notion page. Cleaner than having jig design buried in the protocol doc itself. Say the word and I'll do both.

content.text:
Let me recalculate with your constraints.

## Energy with 230 mm max drop

For ~15 g single weight at 230 mm: KE = ½ × 0.015 × (√(2×9.81×0.23))² = **0.034 J**. That's only ~3× the original tiny proposal — not enough margin at 2.5 m.

**Fix: stack the weights.** Fishing weights stack cheaply — you can build any total mass.

| Total mass | KE @ 230 mm | Estimated peak signal at 0.5 m / 1.5 m / 2.5 m | SNR margin vs typical bathroom noise (~0.002 g RMS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 g (1×) | 0.034 J | ~0.008 / 0.003 / 0.001 g | 12 dB / 3 dB / **buried** |
| 60 g (4×) | 0.135 J | ~0.03 / 0.01 / 0.003 g | 24 / 14 / 4 dB |
| 120 g (8×) | 0.270 J | ~0.06 / 0.02 / 0.006 g | 30 / 20 / 10 dB |
| 180 g (12×) | 0.405 J | ~0.09 / 0.03 / 0.009 g | 33 / 23 / 13 dB |

**Recommended target: ~120 g total mass** (8× 15g weights) for a comfortable 10 dB SNR margin at 2.5 m. If you can comfortably stack 12, even better.

## Design for stacked weights — a "puck" inside a tube

You don't want to drop loose stacked weights — they don't fall together. Solution: pack them into a small 3D-printed shell so they behave as one rigid mass.

```
                  pull-pin (1mm steel rod / paperclip)
                       ↓
                  ╔════╪════════╪════╗
                  ║    │ █████ │    ║ ← PLA puck shell rests on pin
                  ║    └───────┘    ║   (lead weights inside, taped flat)
                  ║                  ║
                  ║                  ║
                  ║   230 mm drop    ║
                  ║                  ║
                  ║                  ║
                  ╚══════════════════╝
                ╔════════════════════════╗
                ║       base plate       ║
                ║  (open hole below tube)║
                ╚════╤══════════════╤════╝
                     ▼              ▼
       ════════════════════════════════ ← tile
                       ↑
              Puck's flat PLA bottom hits tile here
```

## The "puck" — key design point

The puck is a tiny 3D-printed cylindrical shell. The lead fishing weights go *inside* it. The puck's PLA bottom is what hits the tile.

Why this matters:
- **Repeatable striking face**: every drop, the same flat PLA disc contacts the tile. (Loose lead would land in random orientations.)
- **No tile marking**: PLA on porcelain leaves no marks. Lead on porcelain leaves gray transfer.
- **Hard-on-hard impact**: PLA is stiff enough for short contact time (~0.3 ms), giving spectrum out to ~1.5 kHz — more than enough for our 5–200 Hz band.
- **Replaceable**: when the bottom wears after 100+ drops, print a new shell. Lead weights are reused.

### Puck dimensions

For 8× 15g weights (120g) of lead (density 11.3 g/cm³ → volume ~10.6 cm³):

| Dimension | Value |
|---|---|
| Outer diameter | 25 mm |
| Outer height | 30 mm |
| Wall thickness | 2 mm |
| Bottom plate thickness | 3 mm (this is the impact face — make it solid) |
| Top opening | 21 mm dia (slip the weights in, close with a friction-fit cap or just tape) |

Print: 4 walls, **100% infill on the bottom 5 mm** (rigid impact face), 30% gyroid for the rest.

## Tube dimensions

| Dimension | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tube ID | 27 mm | Puck OD (25) + 2 mm clearance — slides smoothly, doesn't wobble |
| Tube wall | 3 mm | Rigid enough that the tube doesn't ring |
| Tube length | 270 mm | 230 mm drop + 40 mm clearance for puck + pin at top |
| Base plate | 70 mm dia × 4 mm, open center | Stable footing on tile; central hole lets puck exit cleanly |
| Pin holes | 1.2 mm dia, 230 mm above inner bottom of tube, opposite sides | For pull-pin |

Print orientation: tube vertical on build plate (long axis = build Z). Slow first layer for smooth interior. Iron the top layer of the base plate if available.

## Component cost — your existing parts + ~$1 print

| Part | What | You already have? |
|---|---|---|
| 8× 15g fishing weights (120g total) | Mass | ✓ (you have them) |
| PLA puck shell | 3D print, ~3 g filament | print |
| PLA tube + base | 3D print, ~30 g filament | print |
| Pin | Bent paperclip or 1 mm steel rod | hardware drawer |
| Tape | To close the puck top + secure weights inside | anything |
| Bubble level (optional) | Tube-vertical check | optional |

**Total cost: essentially the filament.**

## Validation before trusting any data

Same as before — run a 10-drop CoV test at 1.0 m from sensor:

| CoV across 10 drops | Verdict |
|---|---|
| < 5% | Excellent. Proceed. |
| 5–10% | Acceptable. Check: puck slides freely (not jamming)? Pin pulled smoothly? Tube vertical? |
| 10–20% | Investigate before using. |
| > 20% | Don't use. Most likely cause: puck wobble in tube → tape or shim it tighter, or print a new puck with 0.5 mm more OD. |

## Fallback for 2.5 m

If even with 120 g / 230 mm the SNR at 2.5 m is borderline (< 10 dB), two no-build options:

1. **Coherent averaging**: bump N from 5 to 15 drops at 2.5 m. That's another 5 dB SNR for free, thanks to the jig's repeatability (the impulses line up well in time, so averaging works).
2. **Use catfood-bag drop (Phase B4) for 2.5 m IR fitting**: B4 already drops at 2.5 m × 10 with ~5 J of energy. The contact time is longer (~50 ms vs 0.3 ms) → spectrum only covers 5–50 Hz, but that captures the low-frequency floor modes we care most about for fall detection. The jig's broadband data at 0.5 m / 1.5 m fits the mid-frequency content; the catfood at 2.5 m fits the spatial decay.

This actually argues that **the jig and the catfood are complementary**, not redundant — the jig nails the broadband near-field response, the catfood nails the low-frequency far-field response. Both useful.

---

Want me to put this jig design in `docs/impulse_jig_design.md` + a Notion subpage so it's a referenceable artifact?

lastPrompt: should we consider adding a motor and a auto release system so when testing on the ground, human operator can be easier and will not cause vibration?

content.text:
Good question, and the answer is **not yet — but staged for later if needed**.

## The trade-off

A motorized release gives you:
- ✓ Operator out of the vibration zone (the main reason you'd want it)
- ✓ Hands-free trigger
- ✓ Sub-ms onset timestamp via co-recorded trigger signal

But it costs:
- ✗ Build complexity (solenoid + driver + power + wiring)
- ✗ The solenoid itself clicks — needs vibration isolation from the jig stand or it contaminates the signal
- ✗ Doesn't solve the *reload* problem — operator still has to walk back to reset the puck after each drop, which is when most of the "operator presence" actually happens anyway

## The cheaper alternative that gets you 80% of the benefit

**Long string pull**, no electronics:

```
   [jig with pin]──────────string (3 m)──────────[operator outside doorway]
                                                          │
                                                  pulls the string,
                                                  pin slides out,
                                                  puck drops
```

This achieves the main signal-quality goal — **operator is far from the sensor during the impulse event** — at the cost of one length of fishing line. The operator's footsteps to/from the jig happen *between* drops, with a 2 s wait before each release lets the floor settle.

Cost: $0 (you have fishing line already, you have fishing weights).

## The honest comparison

| Approach | Cost | Build time | Operator-during-drop in room? | Operator-during-reload in room? | Per-drop convenience |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Manual pin pull at the jig** | $0 | 0 min | YES (worst) | yes | medium |
| **String pull from outside** | $0 | 5 min | **no** (best with zero electronics) | yes (unavoidable) | medium |
| **Servo release + button** | ~$5 | 1 hour | no | yes | high |
| **Servo release + BLE remote** | ~$15 | 2 hour | no | yes | highest |
| **Solenoid release + remote** | ~$10 | 1 hour | no | yes | high |

The line that matters is **column 4** — "operator in room during the drop." String pull already gets you "no." Motorized adds convenience and a clean trigger signal, but not signal quality, since the reload still requires walking back anyway.

## Recommended staged path

1. **Build the manual pin jig + long string** first (this week, $0). Use it.
2. **Run an operator-presence test**: 10 drops with operator standing 2 m from sensor pulling a 50 cm string vs 10 drops with operator pulling from 3 m outside the doorway. Compare noise floor of pre-impulse window between conditions.
   - If difference is < 3 dB: string pull is fine, save the engineering.
   - If difference is > 6 dB: upgrade to motorized.
3. **If motorized is justified**, go with a **servo + BLE remote** (~$15, ~2 hours):
   - SG90 servo ($3) rotates a small lever that pulls the pin
   - ESP32 or Pi Pico W ($5) drives the servo
   - Trigger via phone (BLE button app like nRF Connect) — no extra hardware
   - Powered from a small USB power bank
   - Servo mounted on a separate stand from the jig, connected by a thin wire/string so the servo's own click is vibration-isolated

## Bonus benefit if you do go motorized

The controller can output a **TTL trigger pulse on each drop** that you can capture on the same recording (if your sensor pipeline has a spare ADC channel or GPIO input). This gives you the *exact* drop time co-recorded with the signal — eliminates the need for onset detection in post-processing and lets you do coherent averaging with sub-sample alignment.

This is the main *technical* reason to motorize, beyond convenience. But it's only worthwhile if the recording chain has a spare channel and if onset detection from the signal itself is proving unreliable (it usually isn't — a ball drop is sharp).

## My recommendation

**Don't build the motor now.** Build the string-pull jig. Run the operator-presence test. The data will tell you whether to upgrade. Probably it'll say "string is fine" — at which point you've saved 2 hours and $15 and have one less battery to remember to charge before each session.

If you start the protocol and string-pull turns out to be awkward (string tangles, pin catches inconsistently, etc.), that's a different "build the motor" reason — convenience, not signal quality. I can spec the servo + BLE version when/if you get there.

"""Build STL files for the impulse jig from the same parameters as impulse_jig.scad.

This is a stopgap until OpenSCAD is installed. The SCAD file is the canonical
parametric source — this Python script generates the same geometry numerically
so we can preview / print without a SCAD installation.

Run:
    /tmp/stl_env/bin/python3 cad/build_jig_stl.py

Outputs:
    cad/jig_tube.stl
    cad/jig_puck.stl
    cad/jig_cap.stl
    cad/jig_preview.png  (rendered preview)
"""
import math
import os
import trimesh
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# ---- parameters (mirror impulse_jig.scad) ----
weight_count          = 8
weight_unit_mass_g    = 15
weight_density_g_cc   = 11.3

drop_height_mm        = 230
tube_extra_top_mm     = 30
tube_wall_mm          = 3
puck_clearance_mm     = 1
pin_dia_mm            = 1.2
base_dia_mm           = 70
base_thickness_mm     = 4

# derived
total_mass_g          = weight_count * weight_unit_mass_g
weight_volume_cc      = total_mass_g / weight_density_g_cc

puck_inner_dia_mm     = 21
puck_inner_radius     = puck_inner_dia_mm / 2
puck_wall_mm          = 2
puck_bottom_mm        = 3
puck_outer_dia_mm     = puck_inner_dia_mm + 2 * puck_wall_mm
puck_required_cavity_cc = weight_volume_cc * 1.15
puck_inner_height_mm  = puck_required_cavity_cc * 1000 / (math.pi * puck_inner_radius ** 2)
puck_total_height_mm  = puck_inner_height_mm + puck_bottom_mm

cap_lip_height_mm     = 4
cap_clearance_mm      = 0.15
cap_top_thickness_mm  = 1.5

tube_id_mm            = puck_outer_dia_mm + 2 * puck_clearance_mm
tube_od_mm            = tube_id_mm + 2 * tube_wall_mm
tube_total_height_mm  = drop_height_mm + tube_extra_top_mm

# ---- print summary ----
v_impact_ms = math.sqrt(2 * 9.81 * drop_height_mm / 1000)
ke_J = 0.5 * (total_mass_g / 1000) * v_impact_ms ** 2
print("=== IMPULSE JIG — derived dimensions ===")
print(f"  total mass: {total_mass_g} g ({weight_count}x {weight_unit_mass_g} g)")
print(f"  puck OD x H: {puck_outer_dia_mm} x {puck_total_height_mm:.1f} mm")
print(f"  tube ID x OD x H: {tube_id_mm} x {tube_od_mm} x {tube_total_height_mm} mm")
print(f"  drop height: {drop_height_mm} mm")
print(f"  impact velocity: {v_impact_ms:.2f} m/s")
print(f"  kinetic energy: {ke_J:.3f} J")

# ---- helpers ----
def cyl(d, h, z=0, sections=64):
    m = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=d/2, height=h, sections=sections)
    m.apply_translation([0, 0, h/2 + z])
    return m

def cyl_at_y(d, h, sections=24):
    # cylinder along Y-axis, centered on origin
    m = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=d/2, height=h, sections=sections)
    # default cylinder is along Z; rotate to align with Y
    m.apply_transform(trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(math.pi/2, [1, 0, 0]))
    return m

# ---- tube assembly ----
print("\nBuilding tube...")
# base plate
base_solid = cyl(base_dia_mm, base_thickness_mm)
base_hole  = cyl(tube_id_mm, base_thickness_mm + 0.2, z=-0.1)
base       = base_solid.difference(base_hole)

# tube
tube_outer = cyl(tube_od_mm, tube_total_height_mm, z=base_thickness_mm)
tube_bore  = cyl(tube_id_mm, tube_total_height_mm + 0.2, z=base_thickness_mm - 0.1)
# pin hole through both walls (along Y axis)
pin_hole = cyl_at_y(pin_dia_mm + 0.3, tube_od_mm + 2)
pin_hole.apply_translation([0, 0, base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm])
tube = tube_outer.difference([tube_bore, pin_hole])

# small witness ring at pin height
ring_outer = cyl(tube_od_mm + 0.8, 0.4, z=base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm)
ring_hole  = cyl(tube_od_mm,       0.6, z=base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm - 0.1)
ring = ring_outer.difference(ring_hole)

tube_assembly = trimesh.util.concatenate([base, tube, ring])
tube_assembly.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_tube.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_tube.stl ({len(tube_assembly.faces)} faces)")

# ---- puck ----
print("\nBuilding puck...")
puck_outer = cyl(puck_outer_dia_mm, puck_total_height_mm)
puck_inner = cyl(puck_inner_dia_mm, puck_total_height_mm - puck_bottom_mm + 0.1, z=puck_bottom_mm)
puck = puck_outer.difference(puck_inner)
puck.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_puck.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_puck.stl ({len(puck.faces)} faces)")

# ---- cap ----
print("\nBuilding cap...")
fit_dia = puck_inner_dia_mm - 2 * cap_clearance_mm
cap_flange = cyl(puck_outer_dia_mm, cap_top_thickness_mm)
cap_lip    = cyl(fit_dia, cap_lip_height_mm, z=-cap_lip_height_mm + 0.01)
cap = trimesh.util.concatenate([cap_flange, cap_lip])
cap.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_cap.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_cap.stl ({len(cap.faces)} faces)")

# ---- preview render ----
print("\nRendering preview...")

# layout: tube on left, puck in middle, cap on right
def shift(mesh, dx):
    m = mesh.copy()
    m.apply_translation([dx, 0, 0])
    return m

x_tube = 0
x_puck = tube_od_mm/2 + 25 + puck_outer_dia_mm/2
x_cap  = x_puck + puck_outer_dia_mm/2 + 15 + puck_outer_dia_mm/2

scene_meshes = [
    ('tube',  tube_assembly,                       'tab:blue'),
    ('puck',  shift(puck, x_puck),                 'tab:orange'),
    ('cap',   shift(cap,  x_cap),                  'tab:green'),
]

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 10))

# 3D view
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 1, projection='3d')
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    tris = m.triangles
    poly = Poly3DCollection(tris, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.05, facecolor=color)
    ax.add_collection3d(poly)
ax.set_xlim(-base_dia_mm/2 - 5, x_cap + puck_outer_dia_mm/2 + 5)
ax.set_ylim(-base_dia_mm/2, base_dia_mm/2)
ax.set_zlim(0, tube_total_height_mm + base_thickness_mm + 5)
try:
    ax.set_box_aspect((x_cap + puck_outer_dia_mm + 10, base_dia_mm, tube_total_height_mm + 10))
except Exception:
    pass
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Y (mm)'); ax.set_zlabel('Z (mm)')
ax.set_title('3D view — tube + puck + cap')
ax.view_init(elev=18, azim=-60)

# Front view (X-Z) — slice all parts
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2)
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    # cut a slice along Y=0 to expose the bore
    try:
        sliced = m.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, 0], plane_normal=[0, 1, 0])
        if sliced is not None:
            # convert to 2D
            slice_2d, _ = sliced.to_2D()
            for poly in slice_2d.polygons_full:
                ax.fill(*poly.exterior.xy, facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5)
                for interior in poly.interiors:
                    ax.fill(*interior.xy, facecolor='white', edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5)
    except Exception:
        # fallback: silhouette
        v = m.vertices
        ax.fill(v[:, 0], v[:, 2], facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.1, alpha=0.2)
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Z (mm)'); ax.set_title('Section through Y=0 (inside view)')
ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Top view (X-Y, looking down)
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 3)
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    # project to X-Y by drawing outlines at multiple Z slices
    # simpler: just outline the vertices in X-Y
    v = m.vertices
    # convex hull in xy as a footprint approximation
    try:
        from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull
        pts = v[:, :2]
        hull = ConvexHull(pts)
        ax.fill(pts[hull.vertices, 0], pts[hull.vertices, 1],
                facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', alpha=0.3, label=name)
    except Exception:
        pass
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Y (mm)'); ax.set_title('Top view (footprints)')
ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(loc='upper right')

# Dimensions text panel
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 4)
ax.axis('off')
info = f"""IMPULSE JIG — design summary

Mass:          {total_mass_g} g  ({weight_count}× {weight_unit_mass_g} g fishing weights)
Drop height:   {drop_height_mm} mm
Impact vel:    {v_impact_ms:.2f} m/s
Energy:        {ke_J:.3f} J

TUBE
  ID:          {tube_id_mm} mm  (puck OD + {2*puck_clearance_mm} mm clearance)
  OD:          {tube_od_mm} mm
  Height:      {tube_total_height_mm} mm  (drop + 30 mm headroom)
  Base plate:  {base_dia_mm} mm dia × {base_thickness_mm} mm thick

PUCK
  OD:          {puck_outer_dia_mm} mm
  ID:          {puck_inner_dia_mm} mm
  Height:      {puck_total_height_mm:.1f} mm
  Bottom:      {puck_bottom_mm} mm SOLID (striking face)

CAP
  OD:          {puck_outer_dia_mm} mm
  Lip dia:     {puck_inner_dia_mm - 2*cap_clearance_mm:.2f} mm (friction fit)
  Lip depth:   {cap_lip_height_mm} mm

PIN
  Dia:         {pin_dia_mm} mm (hole {pin_dia_mm+0.3} mm for paperclip)
  Z position:  {drop_height_mm} mm above tube interior bottom

PRINT SETTINGS
  Tube:  vertical on plate, 4 walls, 30% gyroid, 100% on base
  Puck:  open-face up, 4 walls, 100% bottom
  Cap:   flange-down, 4 walls
"""
ax.text(0.02, 0.98, info, family='monospace', fontsize=10, va='top', ha='left')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_preview.png'), dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
print(f"  saved jig_preview.png")
print("\nDone.")

Markdown is canonical. This Notion page is a reading rendition with variable-control highlights. ## Variable-control legend Used throughout this document — same tags on every section so you can scan quickly. - **CRITICAL** Sensitivity-critical control. If this drifts, the comparison breaks even if everything else is solid. Single most likely failure source. - **HOLD CONSTANT** Must not change within a session or across re-runs. Drift here invalidates comparisons. - **MEASURE & LOG** Allowed to vary but must be recorded (CSV metadata or paper log). Without the value, the data is not analyzable. - **FREE** Can vary freely, no impact on comparability. ## 1 · Purpose Stage 1 left the simulator-only classifier at **50% sensitivity / 44% FP** on real bathroom CSVs. Closing that gap requires fitting each simulator component against real ground truth. This protocol specifies what to measure, in what order, and which `signals.py` parameter each measurement corrects. The impulse test is one piece (the IR-fitting piece); the full plan covers impulse + walk + drop + fall-surrogate + noise so a single bathroom deployment captures everything needed. **Terminology:** *impulse* (not *tap*) is used throughout for the quantitative IR-fitting measurement (A2-A4). "Tap" is reserved for the per-session qualitative mount sanity check (Phase 0), where the result is pass/fail. A quantitative measurement requires a **calibrated impulse source** (a jig); fingernail is NOT acceptable because operator force variability (±50%) contaminates the fit. ## 2 · Hardware setup — what must be held constant
**Item** **Setting** **Variable type** **Why it matters**
MCU + firmware STM32F103C8T6 with `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/代码 - 调节发送频率/USER/main.c` CRITICAL Different firmware → different output format / rate. Comparisons across sessions break.
`INT_MARK` **0** (mandatory, per Amendment 1 P1) CRITICAL Any other value violates the ≥1 kHz rate floor → CSV not admissible as Article I evidence.
Sensor MiniSense 100 (user-confirmed) HOLD CONSTANT Sensor swap → datasheet sensor model invalid. Requires Bill.
Housing `ground_cantilever_housing.stp`, PLA, 100% infill HOLD CONSTANT Re-printing with different infill or material shifts the follow-the-floor resonance.
Preload weight **\~200 g** (range 100–500 g acceptable; pick one and stay) HOLD CONSTANT within a study Different preload → different rocking margin and follow-the-floor resonance.
Transport USART2 (PA2/PA3) → USB-serial @ 115200 baud, FireWater `%.3f\n` CRITICAL Different transport → different buffering → different effective sample rate / drops.
Measured rate Whatever it actually is — typical \~1.38 kHz on USART2-USB MEASURE & LOG Must be in CSV header per Case 1 ruling. **Compute**, don't assume.
Bathroom / tile / device xy Whatever the actual install is MEASURE & LOG Different bathrooms produce different IRs — that's the point of multi-bathroom planning.
## 3 · Sample-rate gate (run before every session) **Gate check (10 s):** capture 10 s of USART2 output, compute `measured_rate_hz = lines / wall_clock_elapsed`. **Must be ≥ 1000 Hz.** If less: abort. INT_MARK is wrong, transport is buffering, or the firmware build is the wrong one. Per Case 1, recordings below 1 kHz are *not admissible* as Article I evidence. ## 4 · Mandatory CSV metadata header (per Case 1) ```javascript # int_mark: 0 CRITICAL # transport: USART2_USB HOLD # measured_rate_hz: 1380 MEASURE # bathroom_id: bathroom_A MEASURE # tile_size_mm: 200x200 MEASURE # device_xy_in_room: "0.3m W wall, 0.5m S wall" MEASURE # preload_mass_g: 200 HOLD # operator: shiyao MEASURE # date: 2026-05-XX MEASURE # session_id: 001 MEASURE # measurement_type: impulse_0.5m MEASURE ``` Missing fields → CSV not admissible. Don't proceed without them. ## 5 · Per-session mount sanity check (\~1 min) 1. Place housing on tile. Confirm baseplate is flush — no rocking when pushing the cap with a finger. 2. Place 200 g weight on top platform. 3. Start USART2 capture. 4. Tap tile 30 cm from housing with a fingernail. **5 taps, \~2 s apart.** 5. Stop capture, inspect: - **Pass:** clean impulse, ringdown \< 50 ms, no inter-tap oscillation - **Fail:** ringdown \> 200 ms (compliant contact), delayed rise (foam), large oscillation between taps (loose preload / rocking baseplate) If fail: alcohol-wipe the tile, re-seat the housing, repeat. **Do not proceed to data collection until sanity check passes.** Bad coupling silently contaminates everything downstream. ## 6 · The protocol as one table (per bathroom) Each row is a discrete measurement. The two highlighted columns are the experimental controls — what must be held constant vs measured/logged for that specific measurement.
**#** **Phase** **Duration** **Measurement & output file** **What must be ****HELD CONSTANT** **What must be ****MEASURED & LOGGED** **Fixes in ****`signals.py`** **Acceptance residual**
0 Sanity 1 min Tap 30 cm × 5 (verify, not saved) tap source (fingernail), tap location (30 cm), preload (200 g) pass/fail observation in operator log n/a — verifies mount only ringdown \< 50 ms, no inter-tap oscillation
A1 Install calib 60 s Quiet baseline, no one in room → `_baseline.csv` no one in room, appliances OFF except vent (if normally on), door state — pick one and stay vent state, door state, time of day `bg_environmental_noise` per-peak amplitudes Real PSD vs sim PSD ±6 dB, 1–500 Hz
A2 Install calib 5 taps Tap at 0.5 m → `_tap_0.5m.csv` CRITICAL tap source (jig or same finger), tap location (marked with tape!), 5 taps ≥ 2 s apart, no other movement in room tap location xy in room, tap force (light/medium/hard) Floor-plate FEA ζ, modal density, near-field gain Per-tap envelope correlation ≥ 0.85
A3 Install calib 5 taps Tap at 1.5 m → `_tap_1.5m.csv` CRITICAL same tap source as A2, location marked with tape, 5 taps ≥ 2 s apart tap location xy, tap force level Same + `REAL_TO_SIM_SCALE` (spatial decay) Ringdown τ ±30%
A4 Install calib 5 taps Tap at 2.5 m → `_tap_2.5m.csv` CRITICAL same as A2/A3 tap location xy, tap force level Same + far-field decay Same
A5 Install calib 60 s Calibration walk → `_walk.csv` one operator, normal pace (\~2 steps/s), footwear (barefoot / socks / sole) — pick one and stay for the whole study operator weight (kg), footwear, rough path description `_footstep_force_profile` peak, contact time Peak mean ±20%, cadence KS p \> 0.05
B1 Events \~5 min Water bottle drops × 15 (0.5/1.5/2.5 m × 5) → `_drop_water.csv` CRITICAL drop height (waist \~1 m, measure once with a stick and keep it), same bottle (mass + fill level), orientation at release (cap up) bottle mass (g with current fill), drop height (m), drop location xy `drop_trajectory` rigid `rebound_pattern` (COR, multi-impact spacing) Multi-peak count ±1, decay corr ≥ 0.80
B2 Events \~3 min Phone drops × 10 → `_drop_phone.csv` same phone, same drop height as B1, same orientation (screen up) phone mass (g), drop height, drop location xy Same, lower-mass rigid Same
B3 Events \~3 min Glass drops × 10 → `_drop_glass.csv` same glass type each time (or label per glass), same drop height, drop into contained area glass mass (g), drop height, drop location xy, did it break? (yes/no) `drop_trajectory` `shatter` pattern (multi-impact) Same
B4 Events \~10 min Catfood-bag drops × 30 (0.5/1.5/2.5 m × 10; 5 of the 1.5m with body-in-path) → `_fall_catfood.csv` CRITICAL same catfood bag (mass + fill), drop height (waist), body-in-path means operator stands DIRECTLY between drop point and sensor bag mass (g), drop height, drop xy, body-in-path? yes/no, operator weight `fall_trajectory` peak + `body_absorption_db` (currently 5 dB guess) Body-in-vs-out amplitude ratio ±2 dB
B5 Events \~5 min Slow-slump surrogate × 10 → `_fall_slump.csv` same heavy bag (\~10 kg), lowered slowly by hand to floor (not dropped) — target descent time (e.g. 2 s) and try to match it bag mass, descent time (s), descent location xy `fall_slump` two-stage profile (rumble onset + impact) Visual match in plot review
B6 Events 5 min Extra walking → `_walk_extra.csv` same operator + footwear as A5 vary the paces deliberately (slow / normal / fast) and log time-windows of each Walking cadence statistics (augments A5) Cadence distribution coverage
B7 Noise 60 s Shower running → `_noise_shower.csv` water on full, no operator movement, door state same as A1 flow rate setting (low/med/high), water temperature (hot/cold) if relevant `noise_shower` PSD amplitudes Per-source PSD ±6 dB
B8 Noise 60 s Vent on → `_noise_vent.csv` vent on at full speed, no other source vent fan rating (W or m³/h) if known `noise_vent` PSD amplitudes Same
B9 Noise 5 flushes Toilet flush × 5 → `_noise_flush.csv` same toilet, wait for refill between flushes, \~30 s gap flush-to-flush gap (s), tank refill duration (s) `noise_flush` transient amplitude + duration Same
B10 Noise 60 s + spin-up Washer (if applicable) → `_noise_washer.csv` washer cycle stage (agitate vs spin), load size repeatable across studies cycle stage, load type, distance from bathroom (m) `noise_washer_local` / `_neighbor` PSD Same
— Log continuous Handwritten / phone-notes labels → `_log.md` log format (timestamp + class + distance + body-in-path + anomaly per line) everything n/a — labeling n/a
**Total per-bathroom time:** \~50–60 min active + 5 min calibration. One session, one device deploy, one operator. ## 7 · Variables that matter most — don't change mid-study **If you change any of these between A-phase and B-phase, or between sessions in the same bathroom, your data is not comparable. Pick once and stick:** - CRITICAL `INT_MARK` value (must stay 0) - CRITICAL impulse source = calibrated jig (NOT fingernail; same jig across A2/A3/A4) - CRITICAL impulse locations (marked with tape, kept across re-installs) - CRITICAL operator footwear (barefoot / socks / sole) across A5 + B6 - CRITICAL drop height across B1/B2/B3/B4 - CRITICAL "body in path" means operator *directly* between drop and sensor — not off-axis - HOLD preload weight (\~200 g, no swap mid-study) - HOLD housing (don't re-print between sessions) - HOLD sensor (no swap) - HOLD door state during baseline + noise recordings - HOLD bathroom appliance state during baseline (everything OFF except what's normally on) **Measure & log (allowed to vary):** - `measured_rate_hz` per session - bag / bottle / phone / glass mass - operator weight (kg) - tile size + device xy in room - drop locations xy - per-event anomalies (bounced off wall, wet floor, etc.) **Free to vary, no impact:** - time of day (within reason — avoid 3 AM dead silence vs 9 AM neighbor noise extremes) - ambient temperature (within room range) - humidity (within bathroom-normal range) ## 8 · After data — the correction loop
**Step** **Who** **What** **Output**
1 Operator Run section 6 on bathroom A `data/bathroom_A/*.csv`
2 Claude Draft fit scripts (`fit_floor_ir.py`, `fit_footstep.py`, `fit_drop_rebound.py`, `fit_body_absorption.py`, `fit_confuser_noise.py`) and a single Bill: *Sim-to-real v3 corrections from bathroom_A* Bill draft + fit scripts
3 Judicial hearing Debate the Bill Case ruling
4 Claude If passed: apply fits to `signals.py`, retrain classifier, rerun sim-to-real v3 Updated `signals.py`, `algorithm.py`, `scripts/sim_to_real_test_v3.py` output
5 Decision gate Inspect v3 vs trigger criteria below "Stay at 1 bathroom" or "Expand to 3"
## 9 · The expand-to-3 trigger (pre-committed)
**v3 result on bathroom A** **Decision** **Why**
Sens ≥ 80%, FP ≤ 10% **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Correction worked here, but need to prove not just over-fit to one tile
Sens 60–80% or FP 10–25% **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Structure looks OK but needs more data
Sens \< 60% or FP \> 25% **Stay at 1, draft simulator-structure Bills** Extra data won't fix a wrong-shaped simulator; revisit modeling assumptions (e.g. multi-tile mosaic, FEA mode selection)
Tap-test repeatability (A2–A4) corr \< 0.7 across the 5 repeats **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Mount / tile coupling unstable — need to see if it's bathroom A or general
## 10 · Open questions before first execution 1. **Impulse source — jig is required, not optional.** Fingernail tap is operator-dependent (±50%) and is NOT acceptable for A2–A4 because the result is fit quantitatively. Required: a calibrated impulse jig (drop a known mass from a fixed height through a vertical tube). Open sizing question per ambient-noise analysis: 10 g ball / 100 mm may be too quiet at 2.5 m; consider 100 g ball / 200 mm, or use the catfood-bag drop (Phase B4) itself as the calibrated IR-fitting impulse. Decision pending. 2. **Sample-rate metadata.** Recommend inline: record session wall-clock start + CSV row count, derive rate post-hoc. 3. **Storage path.** `data/` symlinked outside repo with `.gitignore` to avoid bloating git with large CSVs. 4. **Legacy CSV admission.** Existing `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/bathroom_testing/{catfood,water,step}_201505.csv` should be migrated under `data/bathroom_legacy/` with metadata headers retro-fitted (operator-attested, not measured). Flag the asymmetry in any v3 report. 5. **Event segmentation tool.** Phase B produces 30-minute CSVs with discrete events. Need a tool (script or simple GUI) to extract event windows from log timestamps. Build alongside Phase B execution. --- **Canonical source:** `docs/data_collection_protocol.md` in the `crucible_lite` repo, branch `piezo_fall`. See also `docs/data_collection_protocol.html` for a styled standalone reading rendition. "}

content.subject: Classifier comparison: RF-8 vs RF-13 vs SVM-13
content.description: RF-13 wins: 89.6% sens / 4.12% FP. RF-8: 90.4% / 6.50%. SVM-13: 81.2% / 11.12% (collapsed on walking). New features cut FP rate ~36% at -0.8% sensitivity cost.

content.subject: Cache L1 (IR), L2 (samples), L3 (features) for fast iteration

Markdown is canonical. This Notion page is a reading rendition with variable-control highlights. ## Variable-control legend Used throughout this document — same tags on every section so you can scan quickly. - **CRITICAL** Sensitivity-critical control. If this drifts, the comparison breaks even if everything else is solid. Single most likely failure source. - **HOLD CONSTANT** Must not change within a session or across re-runs. Drift here invalidates comparisons. - **MEASURE & LOG** Allowed to vary but must be recorded (CSV metadata or paper log). Without the value, the data is not analyzable. - **FREE** Can vary freely, no impact on comparability. ## 1 · Purpose Stage 1 left the simulator-only classifier at **50% sensitivity / 44% FP** on real bathroom CSVs. Closing that gap requires fitting each simulator component against real ground truth. This protocol specifies what to measure, in what order, and which `signals.py` parameter each measurement corrects. The impulse test is one piece (the IR-fitting piece); the full plan covers impulse + walk + drop + fall-surrogate + noise so a single bathroom deployment captures everything needed. **Terminology:** *impulse* (not *tap*) is used throughout for the quantitative IR-fitting measurement (A2-A4). "Tap" is reserved for the per-session qualitative mount sanity check (Phase 0), where the result is pass/fail. A quantitative measurement requires a **calibrated impulse source** (a jig); fingernail is NOT acceptable because operator force variability (±50%) contaminates the fit. ## 2 · Hardware setup — what must be held constant
**Item** **Setting** **Variable type** **Why it matters**
MCU + firmware STM32F103C8T6 with `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/代码 - 调节发送频率/USER/main.c` CRITICAL Different firmware → different output format / rate. Comparisons across sessions break.
`INT_MARK` **0** (mandatory, per Amendment 1 P1) CRITICAL Any other value violates the ≥1 kHz rate floor → CSV not admissible as Article I evidence.
Sensor MiniSense 100 (user-confirmed) HOLD CONSTANT Sensor swap → datasheet sensor model invalid. Requires Bill.
Housing `ground_cantilever_housing.stp`, PLA, 100% infill HOLD CONSTANT Re-printing with different infill or material shifts the follow-the-floor resonance.
Preload weight **\~200 g** (range 100–500 g acceptable; pick one and stay) HOLD CONSTANT within a study Different preload → different rocking margin and follow-the-floor resonance.
Transport USART2 (PA2/PA3) → USB-serial @ 115200 baud, FireWater `%.3f\n` CRITICAL Different transport → different buffering → different effective sample rate / drops.
Measured rate Whatever it actually is — typical \~1.38 kHz on USART2-USB MEASURE & LOG Must be in CSV header per Case 1 ruling. **Compute**, don't assume.
Bathroom / tile / device xy Whatever the actual install is MEASURE & LOG Different bathrooms produce different IRs — that's the point of multi-bathroom planning.
## 3 · Sample-rate gate (run before every session) **Gate check (10 s):** capture 10 s of USART2 output, compute `measured_rate_hz = lines / wall_clock_elapsed`. **Must be ≥ 1000 Hz.** If less: abort. INT_MARK is wrong, transport is buffering, or the firmware build is the wrong one. Per Case 1, recordings below 1 kHz are *not admissible* as Article I evidence. ## 4 · Mandatory CSV metadata header (per Case 1) ```javascript # int_mark: 0 CRITICAL # transport: USART2_USB HOLD # measured_rate_hz: 1380 MEASURE # bathroom_id: bathroom_A MEASURE # tile_size_mm: 200x200 MEASURE # device_xy_in_room: "0.3m W wall, 0.5m S wall" MEASURE # preload_mass_g: 200 HOLD # operator: shiyao MEASURE # date: 2026-05-XX MEASURE # session_id: 001 MEASURE # measurement_type: impulse_0.5m MEASURE ``` Missing fields → CSV not admissible. Don't proceed without them. ## 5 · Per-session mount sanity check (\~1 min) 1. Place housing on tile. Confirm baseplate is flush — no rocking when pushing the cap with a finger. 2. Place 200 g weight on top platform. 3. Start USART2 capture. 4. Tap tile 30 cm from housing with a fingernail. **5 taps, \~2 s apart.** 5. Stop capture, inspect: - **Pass:** clean impulse, ringdown \< 50 ms, no inter-tap oscillation - **Fail:** ringdown \> 200 ms (compliant contact), delayed rise (foam), large oscillation between taps (loose preload / rocking baseplate) If fail: alcohol-wipe the tile, re-seat the housing, repeat. **Do not proceed to data collection until sanity check passes.** Bad coupling silently contaminates everything downstream. ## 6 · The protocol as one table (per bathroom) Each row is a discrete measurement. The two highlighted columns are the experimental controls — what must be held constant vs measured/logged for that specific measurement.
**#** **Phase** **Duration** **Measurement & output file** **What must be ****HELD CONSTANT** **What must be ****MEASURED & LOGGED** **Fixes in ****`signals.py`** **Acceptance residual**
0 Sanity 1 min Tap 30 cm × 5 (verify, not saved) tap source (fingernail), tap location (30 cm), preload (200 g) pass/fail observation in operator log n/a — verifies mount only ringdown \< 50 ms, no inter-tap oscillation
A1 Install calib 60 s Quiet baseline, no one in room → `_baseline.csv` no one in room, appliances OFF except vent (if normally on), door state — pick one and stay vent state, door state, time of day `bg_environmental_noise` per-peak amplitudes Real PSD vs sim PSD ±6 dB, 1–500 Hz
A2 Install calib 5 jig drops Impulse at 0.5 m → `_impulse_0.5m.csv` CRITICAL impulse source = calibrated jig (NOT fingernail), location marked with tape, 5 jig drops ≥ 2 s apart, no other movement in room impulse location xy in room, jig parameters (mass, drop height) Floor-plate FEA ζ, modal density, near-field gain Per-impulse envelope correlation ≥ 0.85
A3 Install calib 5 jig drops Impulse at 1.5 m → `_impulse_1.5m.csv` CRITICAL same impulse jig as A2, location marked with tape, 5 jig drops ≥ 2 s apart impulse location xy, jig parameters Same + `REAL_TO_SIM_SCALE` (spatial decay) Ringdown τ ±30%
A4 Install calib 5 jig drops Impulse at 2.5 m → `_impulse_2.5m.csv` CRITICAL same as A2/A3 impulse location xy, jig parameters Same + far-field decay Same
A5 Install calib 60 s Calibration walk → `_walk.csv` one operator, normal pace (\~2 steps/s), footwear (barefoot / socks / sole) — pick one and stay for the whole study operator weight (kg), footwear, rough path description `_footstep_force_profile` peak, contact time Peak mean ±20%, cadence KS p \> 0.05
B1 Events \~5 min Water bottle drops × 15 (0.5/1.5/2.5 m × 5) → `_drop_water.csv` CRITICAL drop height (waist \~1 m, measure once with a stick and keep it), same bottle (mass + fill level), orientation at release (cap up) bottle mass (g with current fill), drop height (m), drop location xy `drop_trajectory` rigid `rebound_pattern` (COR, multi-impact spacing) Multi-peak count ±1, decay corr ≥ 0.80
B2 Events \~3 min Phone drops × 10 → `_drop_phone.csv` same phone, same drop height as B1, same orientation (screen up) phone mass (g), drop height, drop location xy Same, lower-mass rigid Same
B3 Events \~3 min Glass drops × 10 → `_drop_glass.csv` same glass type each time (or label per glass), same drop height, drop into contained area glass mass (g), drop height, drop location xy, did it break? (yes/no) `drop_trajectory` `shatter` pattern (multi-impact) Same
B4 Events \~10 min Catfood-bag drops × 30 (0.5/1.5/2.5 m × 10; 5 of the 1.5m with body-in-path) → `_fall_catfood.csv` CRITICAL same catfood bag (mass + fill), drop height (waist), body-in-path means operator stands DIRECTLY between drop point and sensor bag mass (g), drop height, drop xy, body-in-path? yes/no, operator weight `fall_trajectory` peak + `body_absorption_db` (currently 5 dB guess) Body-in-vs-out amplitude ratio ±2 dB
B5 Events \~5 min Slow-slump surrogate × 10 → `_fall_slump.csv` same heavy bag (\~10 kg), lowered slowly by hand to floor (not dropped) — target descent time (e.g. 2 s) and try to match it bag mass, descent time (s), descent location xy `fall_slump` two-stage profile (rumble onset + impact) Visual match in plot review
B6 Events 5 min Extra walking → `_walk_extra.csv` same operator + footwear as A5 vary the paces deliberately (slow / normal / fast) and log time-windows of each Walking cadence statistics (augments A5) Cadence distribution coverage
B7 Noise 60 s Shower running → `_noise_shower.csv` water on full, no operator movement, door state same as A1 flow rate setting (low/med/high), water temperature (hot/cold) if relevant `noise_shower` PSD amplitudes Per-source PSD ±6 dB
B8 Noise 60 s Vent on → `_noise_vent.csv` vent on at full speed, no other source vent fan rating (W or m³/h) if known `noise_vent` PSD amplitudes Same
B9 Noise 5 flushes Toilet flush × 5 → `_noise_flush.csv` same toilet, wait for refill between flushes, \~30 s gap flush-to-flush gap (s), tank refill duration (s) `noise_flush` transient amplitude + duration Same
B10 Noise 60 s + spin-up Washer (if applicable) → `_noise_washer.csv` washer cycle stage (agitate vs spin), load size repeatable across studies cycle stage, load type, distance from bathroom (m) `noise_washer_local` / `_neighbor` PSD Same
— Log continuous Handwritten / phone-notes labels → `_log.md` log format (timestamp + class + distance + body-in-path + anomaly per line) everything n/a — labeling n/a
**Total per-bathroom time:** \~50–60 min active + 5 min calibration. One session, one device deploy, one operator. ## 7 · Variables that matter most — don't change mid-study **If you change any of these between A-phase and B-phase, or between sessions in the same bathroom, your data is not comparable. Pick once and stick:** - CRITICAL `INT_MARK` value (must stay 0) - CRITICAL impulse source = calibrated jig (NOT fingernail; same jig across A2/A3/A4) - CRITICAL impulse locations (marked with tape, kept across re-installs) - CRITICAL operator footwear (barefoot / socks / sole) across A5 + B6 - CRITICAL drop height across B1/B2/B3/B4 - CRITICAL "body in path" means operator *directly* between drop and sensor — not off-axis - HOLD preload weight (\~200 g, no swap mid-study) - HOLD housing (don't re-print between sessions) - HOLD sensor (no swap) - HOLD door state during baseline + noise recordings - HOLD bathroom appliance state during baseline (everything OFF except what's normally on) **Measure & log (allowed to vary):** - `measured_rate_hz` per session - bag / bottle / phone / glass mass - operator weight (kg) - tile size + device xy in room - drop locations xy - per-event anomalies (bounced off wall, wet floor, etc.) **Free to vary, no impact:** - time of day (within reason — avoid 3 AM dead silence vs 9 AM neighbor noise extremes) - ambient temperature (within room range) - humidity (within bathroom-normal range) ## 8 · After data — the correction loop
**Step** **Who** **What** **Output**
1 Operator Run section 6 on bathroom A `data/bathroom_A/*.csv`
2 Claude Draft fit scripts (`fit_floor_ir.py`, `fit_footstep.py`, `fit_drop_rebound.py`, `fit_body_absorption.py`, `fit_confuser_noise.py`) and a single Bill: *Sim-to-real v3 corrections from bathroom_A* Bill draft + fit scripts
3 Judicial hearing Debate the Bill Case ruling
4 Claude If passed: apply fits to `signals.py`, retrain classifier, rerun sim-to-real v3 Updated `signals.py`, `algorithm.py`, `scripts/sim_to_real_test_v3.py` output
5 Decision gate Inspect v3 vs trigger criteria below "Stay at 1 bathroom" or "Expand to 3"
## 9 · The expand-to-3 trigger (pre-committed)
**v3 result on bathroom A** **Decision** **Why**
Sens ≥ 80%, FP ≤ 10% **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Correction worked here, but need to prove not just over-fit to one tile
Sens 60–80% or FP 10–25% **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Structure looks OK but needs more data
Sens \< 60% or FP \> 25% **Stay at 1, draft simulator-structure Bills** Extra data won't fix a wrong-shaped simulator; revisit modeling assumptions (e.g. multi-tile mosaic, FEA mode selection)
Impulse-test repeatability (A2–A4) corr \< 0.7 across the 5 repeats **Expand to 3 bathrooms** Mount / tile coupling unstable — need to see if it's bathroom A or general
## 10 · Open questions before first execution 1. **Impulse source — jig is required, not optional.** Fingernail tap is operator-dependent (±50%) and is NOT acceptable for A2–A4 because the result is fit quantitatively. Required: a calibrated impulse jig (drop a known mass from a fixed height through a vertical tube). Open sizing question per ambient-noise analysis: 10 g ball / 100 mm may be too quiet at 2.5 m; consider 100 g ball / 200 mm, or use the catfood-bag drop (Phase B4) itself as the calibrated IR-fitting impulse. Decision pending. 2. **Sample-rate metadata.** Recommend inline: record session wall-clock start + CSV row count, derive rate post-hoc. 3. **Storage path.** `data/` symlinked outside repo with `.gitignore` to avoid bloating git with large CSVs. 4. **Legacy CSV admission.** Existing `~/Documents/piezo_circuit/bathroom_testing/{catfood,water,step}_201505.csv` should be migrated under `data/bathroom_legacy/` with metadata headers retro-fitted (operator-attested, not measured). Flag the asymmetry in any v3 report. 5. **Event segmentation tool.** Phase B produces 30-minute CSVs with discrete events. Need a tool (script or simple GUI) to extract event windows from log timestamps. Build alongside Phase B execution. --- **Canonical source:** `docs/data_collection_protocol.md` in the `crucible_lite` repo, branch `piezo_fall`. See also `docs/data_collection_protocol.html` for a styled standalone reading rendition. "}

## CAD summary — what got produced

`cad/` directory now contains:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **`impulse_jig.scad`** | **Canonical parametric source.** Open in OpenSCAD (free), edit weight count / drop height / clearances at the top, render any part, export STL. |

| `jig_puck.stl` | Cylindrical shell (OD 25 mm, H 38 mm) that holds 8× 15g fishing weights = 120 g total. **3 mm solid PLA bottom = the striking face**. |

| `build_jig_stl.py` | Python stopgap that generated those STLs via trimesh (since OpenSCAD wasn't installed in this env). Run if you want to regenerate from the same parameters. |
| `jig_preview.png` | 4-panel render: 3D view, section through Y=0 (shows the bore and pin hole), top-view footprints, dimensions panel. |

## Specs at default config

- Total mass: **120 g** (8× 15g weights)
- Drop height: **230 mm**
- Impact velocity: 2.12 m/s
- **Kinetic energy: 0.27 J** (~30× the original 10g/100mm proposal)
- Print time estimate: tube ~3h, puck ~30 min, cap ~10 min on a normal FDM printer at 0.2 mm layer height

## To print

Slice each STL separately (or all on one plate):
- **Tube**: print vertical (long axis = build Z), 4 walls, 30% gyroid infill, 100% on first 5 mm of base
- **Puck**: print with open face up, 4 walls, 100% bottom infill
- **Cap**: print flange-side down, 4 walls

PLA at 100% infill on the puck bottom is what gives you the rigid striking face. If you want to alter mass / drop height / clearances, edit the `.scad` parameters and re-render — everything downstream auto-recomputes.

If you want me to add a second tube variant (e.g. for a heavier escalation: 200g weight at 230mm = 0.45 J) or a remote-string-release retainer, let me know.

"""Build STL files for the impulse jig from the same parameters as impulse_jig.scad.

This is a stopgap until OpenSCAD is installed. The SCAD file is the canonical
parametric source — this Python script generates the same geometry numerically
so we can preview / print without a SCAD installation.

Run:
    /tmp/stl_env/bin/python3 cad/build_jig_stl.py

Outputs:
    cad/jig_tube.stl
    cad/jig_puck.stl
    cad/jig_cap.stl
    cad/jig_preview.png  (rendered preview)
"""
import math
import os
import trimesh
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# ---- parameters (mirror impulse_jig.scad) ----
weight_count          = 8
weight_unit_mass_g    = 15
weight_density_g_cc   = 11.3

drop_height_mm        = 230
tube_extra_top_mm     = 30
tube_wall_mm          = 3
puck_clearance_mm     = 1
pin_dia_mm            = 1.2
base_dia_mm           = 70
base_thickness_mm     = 4

# derived
total_mass_g          = weight_count * weight_unit_mass_g
weight_volume_cc      = total_mass_g / weight_density_g_cc

puck_inner_dia_mm     = 21
puck_inner_radius     = puck_inner_dia_mm / 2
puck_wall_mm          = 2

"""Build STL files for the impulse jig from the same parameters as impulse_jig.scad.

This is a stopgap until OpenSCAD is installed. The SCAD file is the canonical
parametric source — this Python script generates the same geometry numerically
so we can preview / print without a SCAD installation.

Run:
    /tmp/stl_env/bin/python3 cad/build_jig_stl.py

Outputs:
    cad/jig_tube.stl
    cad/jig_puck.stl
    cad/jig_cap.stl
    cad/jig_preview.png  (rendered preview)
"""
import math
import os
import trimesh
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# ---- parameters (mirror impulse_jig.scad) ----
weight_count          = 8
weight_unit_mass_g    = 15
weight_density_g_cc   = 11.3

drop_height_mm        = 230
tube_extra_top_mm     = 16   # tuned for Bambu X1C Z=256mm (total height 250mm)
tube_wall_mm          = 3
puck_clearance_mm     = 1
pin_dia_mm            = 1.2
base_dia_mm           = 70
base_thickness_mm     = 4
funnel_extra_dia_mm   = 5    # loading-funnel widening at tube top
funnel_depth_mm       = 5

# derived
total_mass_g          = weight_count * weight_unit_mass_g
weight_volume_cc      = total_mass_g / weight_density_g_cc

puck_inner_dia_mm     = 21
puck_inner_radius     = puck_inner_dia_mm / 2
puck_wall_mm          = 2
puck_bottom_mm        = 3
puck_outer_dia_mm     = puck_inner_dia_mm + 2 * puck_wall_mm
puck_required_cavity_cc = weight_volume_cc * 1.15
puck_inner_height_mm  = puck_required_cavity_cc * 1000 / (math.pi * puck_inner_radius ** 2)
puck_total_height_mm  = puck_inner_height_mm + puck_bottom_mm

cap_lip_height_mm     = 4
cap_clearance_mm      = 0.15
cap_top_thickness_mm  = 1.5

tube_id_mm            = puck_outer_dia_mm + 2 * puck_clearance_mm
tube_od_mm            = tube_id_mm + 2 * tube_wall_mm
tube_total_height_mm  = drop_height_mm + tube_extra_top_mm

# ---- print summary ----
v_impact_ms = math.sqrt(2 * 9.81 * drop_height_mm / 1000)
ke_J = 0.5 * (total_mass_g / 1000) * v_impact_ms ** 2
total_print_height_mm = tube_total_height_mm + base_thickness_mm
print("=== IMPULSE JIG — derived dimensions ===")
print(f"  total mass: {total_mass_g} g ({weight_count}x {weight_unit_mass_g} g)")
print(f"  puck OD x H: {puck_outer_dia_mm} x {puck_total_height_mm:.1f} mm")
print(f"  tube ID x OD x H: {tube_id_mm} x {tube_od_mm} x {tube_total_height_mm} mm")
print(f"  TOTAL PRINT HEIGHT (tube+base): {total_print_height_mm} mm  "
      f"[X1C Z=256mm -> margin: {256 - total_print_height_mm} mm]")
print(f"  drop height: {drop_height_mm} mm")
print(f"  impact velocity: {v_impact_ms:.2f} m/s")
print(f"  kinetic energy: {ke_J:.3f} J")

# ---- helpers ----
def cyl(d, h, z=0, sections=64):
    m = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=d/2, height=h, sections=sections)
    m.apply_translation([0, 0, h/2 + z])
    return m

def cyl_at_y(d, h, sections=24):
    # cylinder along Y-axis, centered on origin
    m = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=d/2, height=h, sections=sections)
    # default cylinder is along Z; rotate to align with Y
    m.apply_transform(trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(math.pi/2, [1, 0, 0]))
    return m

# ---- tube assembly ----
print("\nBuilding tube...")
# base plate
base_solid = cyl(base_dia_mm, base_thickness_mm)
base_hole  = cyl(tube_id_mm, base_thickness_mm + 0.2, z=-0.1)
base       = base_solid.difference(base_hole)

# tube
tube_outer = cyl(tube_od_mm, tube_total_height_mm, z=base_thickness_mm)
tube_bore  = cyl(tube_id_mm, tube_total_height_mm + 0.2, z=base_thickness_mm - 0.1)
# pin hole through both walls (along Y axis)
pin_hole = cyl_at_y(pin_dia_mm + 0.3, tube_od_mm + 2)
pin_hole.apply_translation([0, 0, base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm])
tube = tube_outer.difference([tube_bore, pin_hole])

# small witness ring at pin height
ring_outer = cyl(tube_od_mm + 0.8, 0.4, z=base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm)
ring_hole  = cyl(tube_od_mm,       0.6, z=base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm - 0.1)
ring = ring_outer.difference(ring_hole)

tube_assembly = trimesh.util.concatenate([base, tube, ring])
tube_assembly.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_tube.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_tube.stl ({len(tube_assembly.faces)} faces)")

# ---- puck ----
print("\nBuilding puck...")
puck_outer = cyl(puck_outer_dia_mm, puck_total_height_mm)
puck_inner = cyl(puck_inner_dia_mm, puck_total_height_mm - puck_bottom_mm + 0.1, z=puck_bottom_mm)
puck = puck_outer.difference(puck_inner)
puck.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_puck.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_puck.stl ({len(puck.faces)} faces)")

# ---- cap ----
print("\nBuilding cap...")
fit_dia = puck_inner_dia_mm - 2 * cap_clearance_mm
cap_flange = cyl(puck_outer_dia_mm, cap_top_thickness_mm)
cap_lip    = cyl(fit_dia, cap_lip_height_mm, z=-cap_lip_height_mm + 0.01)
cap = trimesh.util.concatenate([cap_flange, cap_lip])
cap.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_cap.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_cap.stl ({len(cap.faces)} faces)")

# ---- preview render ----
print("\nRendering preview...")

# layout: tube on left, puck in middle, cap on right
def shift(mesh, dx):
    m = mesh.copy()
    m.apply_translation([dx, 0, 0])
    return m

x_tube = 0
x_puck = tube_od_mm/2 + 25 + puck_outer_dia_mm/2
x_cap  = x_puck + puck_outer_dia_mm/2 + 15 + puck_outer_dia_mm/2

scene_meshes = [
    ('tube',  tube_assembly,                       'tab:blue'),
    ('puck',  shift(puck, x_puck),                 'tab:orange'),
    ('cap',   shift(cap,  x_cap),                  'tab:green'),
]

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 10))

# 3D view
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 1, projection='3d')
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    tris = m.triangles
    poly = Poly3DCollection(tris, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.05, facecolor=color)
    ax.add_collection3d(poly)
ax.set_xlim(-base_dia_mm/2 - 5, x_cap + puck_outer_dia_mm/2 + 5)
ax.set_ylim(-base_dia_mm/2, base_dia_mm/2)
ax.set_zlim(0, tube_total_height_mm + base_thickness_mm + 5)
try:
    ax.set_box_aspect((x_cap + puck_outer_dia_mm + 10, base_dia_mm, tube_total_height_mm + 10))
except Exception:
    pass
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Y (mm)'); ax.set_zlabel('Z (mm)')
ax.set_title('3D view — tube + puck + cap')
ax.view_init(elev=18, azim=-60)

# Front view (X-Z) — slice all parts
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2)
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    # cut a slice along Y=0 to expose the bore
    try:
        sliced = m.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, 0], plane_normal=[0, 1, 0])
        if sliced is not None:
            # convert to 2D
            slice_2d, _ = sliced.to_2D()
            for poly in slice_2d.polygons_full:
                ax.fill(*poly.exterior.xy, facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5)
                for interior in poly.interiors:
                    ax.fill(*interior.xy, facecolor='white', edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5)
    except Exception:
        # fallback: silhouette
        v = m.vertices
        ax.fill(v[:, 0], v[:, 2], facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.1, alpha=0.2)
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Z (mm)'); ax.set_title('Section through Y=0 (inside view)')
ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Top view (X-Y, looking down)
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 3)
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    # project to X-Y by drawing outlines at multiple Z slices
    # simpler: just outline the vertices in X-Y
    v = m.vertices
    # convex hull in xy as a footprint approximation
    try:
        from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull
        pts = v[:, :2]
        hull = ConvexHull(pts)
        ax.fill(pts[hull.vertices, 0], pts[hull.vertices, 1],
                facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', alpha=0.3, label=name)
    except Exception:
        pass
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Y (mm)'); ax.set_title('Top view (footprints)')
ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(loc='upper right')

# Dimensions text panel
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 4)
ax.axis('off')
info = f"""IMPULSE JIG — design summary

Mass:          {total_mass_g} g  ({weight_count}× {weight_unit_mass_g} g fishing weights)
Drop height:   {drop_height_mm} mm
Impact vel:    {v_impact_ms:.2f} m/s

CAP

content.subject: Classifier comparison: RF-8 vs RF-13 vs SVM-13
content.description: RF-13 wins: 89.6% sens / 4.12% FP. RF-8: 90.4% / 6.50%. SVM-13: 81.2% / 11.12% (collapsed on walking). New features cut FP rate ~36% at -0.8% sensitivity cost.

content.subject: Cache L1 (IR), L2 (samples), L3 (features) for fast iteration
content.description: DEFERRED — only worth implementing if iteration resumes. Cache levels L1 (IR), L2 (samples), L3 (features) for fast iteration. Would cut classifier-only iteration from ~12 min to ~5 sec.

content.subject: Hearing for Bill 001 — Amendment 1 sample-rate revision
content.description: Bill 001 enacted with modification — Case 1 ruling: A1 P1 rate floor raised to ≥1.5 kHz (mechanically enforces INT_MARK=0), + mandatory CSV metadata (int_mark, transport, measured_rate_hz). Commit 4bb237c.

content.subject: Confirm deployed sensor = MiniSense 100 (BOM or part marking vs datasheet)
content.description: RESOLVED 2026-05-16. Deployed sensor is NOT a MiniSense 100. Evidence: (1) ~/Documents/piezo_circuit/SENSOR_MOUNTING.md describes a custom-assembled cantilever — 25mm×8mm×28µm bare PVDF strip + 2-10g brass/steel proof mass, base epoxied to floor, resonance 50-500 Hz depending on geometry; (2) BOM lists only conditioning electronics (CA3140/MAX44248 + 100 MΩ bias R48), no commercial sensor module; (3) zero "MiniSense" hits in original repo. The MiniSense 100 assumption originated in our simulator work, not the hardware record. Simulator sensor model fn/ζ/sensitivity require revision via Bill once the actual cantilever is tap-tested.

content.subject: Plan real-to-sim correction data collection (taps + walks + drops + falls)
content.description: Drafted in docs/data_collection_protocol.md (2026-05-16). Single coherent plan covering full real-to-sim correction dataset, not just tap test. Scope: 1 bathroom first with explicit expand-to-3 trigger criteria. Each measurement explicitly tied to a simulator component it fits + acceptance residual. After data collected, fit scripts + simulator updates go through a single Bill ("Sim-to-real v3 corrections").

content.subject: Sim-to-real v2 with corrected tag mapping + distance grouping
content.description: Tag mapping: step→confuser_step, fall→fall_fast (catfood=body fall surrogate), other→confuser_drop_phone (water=rigid drop). Per-distance grouping via peak-sorted. Catfood 1.5m split into unblocked (top 3) and blocked (bottom 3) per drop-human-sensor experimental design. Body-absorption (5 dB) added to fall_trajectory.

"""Build STL files for the impulse jig from the same parameters as impulse_jig.scad.

This is a stopgap until OpenSCAD is installed. The SCAD file is the canonical
parametric source — this Python script generates the same geometry numerically
so we can preview / print without a SCAD installation.

Run:
    /tmp/stl_env/bin/python3 cad/build_jig_stl.py

Outputs:
    cad/jig_tube.stl
    cad/jig_puck.stl
    cad/jig_cap.stl
    cad/jig_preview.png  (rendered preview)
"""
import math
import os
import trimesh
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# ---- parameters (mirror impulse_jig.scad) ----
weight_count          = 8
weight_unit_mass_g    = 15
weight_density_g_cc   = 11.3

drop_height_mm        = 230
tube_extra_top_mm     = 16   # tuned for Bambu X1C Z=256mm (total height 250mm)
tube_wall_mm          = 3
puck_clearance_mm     = 1
pin_dia_mm            = 1.2
base_dia_mm           = 70
base_thickness_mm     = 4
funnel_extra_dia_mm   = 5    # loading-funnel widening at tube top
funnel_depth_mm       = 5

# derived
total_mass_g          = weight_count * weight_unit_mass_g
weight_volume_cc      = total_mass_g / weight_density_g_cc

puck_inner_dia_mm     = 21
puck_inner_radius     = puck_inner_dia_mm / 2
puck_wall_mm          = 2
puck_bottom_mm        = 3
puck_outer_dia_mm     = puck_inner_dia_mm + 2 * puck_wall_mm
puck_required_cavity_cc = weight_volume_cc * 1.15
puck_inner_height_mm  = puck_required_cavity_cc * 1000 / (math.pi * puck_inner_radius ** 2)
puck_total_height_mm  = puck_inner_height_mm + puck_bottom_mm

cap_lip_height_mm     = 4
cap_clearance_mm      = 0.15
cap_top_thickness_mm  = 1.5

tube_id_mm            = puck_outer_dia_mm + 2 * puck_clearance_mm
tube_od_mm            = tube_id_mm + 2 * tube_wall_mm
tube_total_height_mm  = drop_height_mm + tube_extra_top_mm

# ---- print summary ----
v_impact_ms = math.sqrt(2 * 9.81 * drop_height_mm / 1000)
ke_J = 0.5 * (total_mass_g / 1000) * v_impact_ms ** 2
total_print_height_mm = tube_total_height_mm + base_thickness_mm
print("=== IMPULSE JIG — derived dimensions ===")
print(f"  total mass: {total_mass_g} g ({weight_count}x {weight_unit_mass_g} g)")
print(f"  puck OD x H: {puck_outer_dia_mm} x {puck_total_height_mm:.1f} mm")
print(f"  tube ID x OD x H: {tube_id_mm} x {tube_od_mm} x {tube_total_height_mm} mm")
print(f"  TOTAL PRINT HEIGHT (tube+base): {total_print_height_mm} mm  "
      f"[X1C Z=256mm -> margin: {256 - total_print_height_mm} mm]")
print(f"  drop height: {drop_height_mm} mm")
print(f"  impact velocity: {v_impact_ms:.2f} m/s")
print(f"  kinetic energy: {ke_J:.3f} J")

# ---- helpers ----
def cyl(d, h, z=0, sections=64):
    m = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=d/2, height=h, sections=sections)
    m.apply_translation([0, 0, h/2 + z])
    return m

def cyl_at_y(d, h, sections=24):
    # cylinder along Y-axis, centered on origin
    m = trimesh.creation.cylinder(radius=d/2, height=h, sections=sections)
    # default cylinder is along Z; rotate to align with Y
    m.apply_transform(trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(math.pi/2, [1, 0, 0]))
    return m

# ---- tube assembly ----
print("\nBuilding tube...")
# base plate
base_solid = cyl(base_dia_mm, base_thickness_mm)
base_hole  = cyl(tube_id_mm, base_thickness_mm + 0.2, z=-0.1)
base       = base_solid.difference(base_hole)

# tube
tube_outer = cyl(tube_od_mm, tube_total_height_mm, z=base_thickness_mm)
tube_bore  = cyl(tube_id_mm, tube_total_height_mm + 0.2, z=base_thickness_mm - 0.1)
# loading funnel at top (truncated cone widening the bore)
funnel = trimesh.creation.cone(radius=(tube_id_mm + funnel_extra_dia_mm) / 2,
                                height=funnel_depth_mm + 0.1, sections=64)
# cone() makes a cone with apex up. We want a frustum widening upward.
# Construct as a cylinder difference for simplicity:
funnel_box   = cyl(tube_id_mm + funnel_extra_dia_mm, funnel_depth_mm + 0.1,
                   z=base_thickness_mm + tube_total_height_mm - funnel_depth_mm)
# Use a tapered approach: subtract a cone-shaped solid
# Easier: just use a slight outward chamfer via a wider cylinder at top
pin_hole = cyl_at_y(pin_dia_mm + 0.3, tube_od_mm + 2)
pin_hole.apply_translation([0, 0, base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm])
tube = tube_outer.difference([tube_bore, funnel_box, pin_hole])

# small witness ring at pin height
ring_outer = cyl(tube_od_mm + 0.8, 0.4, z=base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm)
ring_hole  = cyl(tube_od_mm,       0.6, z=base_thickness_mm + drop_height_mm - 0.1)
ring = ring_outer.difference(ring_hole)

tube_assembly = trimesh.util.concatenate([base, tube, ring])
tube_assembly.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_tube.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_tube.stl ({len(tube_assembly.faces)} faces)")

# ---- puck ----
print("\nBuilding puck...")
puck_outer = cyl(puck_outer_dia_mm, puck_total_height_mm)
puck_inner = cyl(puck_inner_dia_mm, puck_total_height_mm - puck_bottom_mm + 0.1, z=puck_bottom_mm)
puck = puck_outer.difference(puck_inner)
puck.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_puck.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_puck.stl ({len(puck.faces)} faces)")

# ---- cap ----
print("\nBuilding cap...")
fit_dia = puck_inner_dia_mm - 2 * cap_clearance_mm
cap_flange = cyl(puck_outer_dia_mm, cap_top_thickness_mm)
cap_lip    = cyl(fit_dia, cap_lip_height_mm, z=-cap_lip_height_mm + 0.01)
cap = trimesh.util.concatenate([cap_flange, cap_lip])
cap.export(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_cap.stl'))
print(f"  saved jig_cap.stl ({len(cap.faces)} faces)")

# ---- preview render ----
print("\nRendering preview...")

# layout: tube on left, puck in middle, cap on right
def shift(mesh, dx):
    m = mesh.copy()
    m.apply_translation([dx, 0, 0])
    return m

x_tube = 0
x_puck = tube_od_mm/2 + 25 + puck_outer_dia_mm/2
x_cap  = x_puck + puck_outer_dia_mm/2 + 15 + puck_outer_dia_mm/2

scene_meshes = [
    ('tube',  tube_assembly,                       'tab:blue'),
    ('puck',  shift(puck, x_puck),                 'tab:orange'),
    ('cap',   shift(cap,  x_cap),                  'tab:green'),
]

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 10))

# 3D view
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 1, projection='3d')
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    tris = m.triangles
    poly = Poly3DCollection(tris, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.05, facecolor=color)
    ax.add_collection3d(poly)
ax.set_xlim(-base_dia_mm/2 - 5, x_cap + puck_outer_dia_mm/2 + 5)
ax.set_ylim(-base_dia_mm/2, base_dia_mm/2)
ax.set_zlim(0, tube_total_height_mm + base_thickness_mm + 5)
try:
    ax.set_box_aspect((x_cap + puck_outer_dia_mm + 10, base_dia_mm, tube_total_height_mm + 10))
except Exception:
    pass
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Y (mm)'); ax.set_zlabel('Z (mm)')
ax.set_title('3D view — tube + puck + cap')
ax.view_init(elev=18, azim=-60)

# Front view (X-Z) — slice all parts
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2)
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    # cut a slice along Y=0 to expose the bore
    try:
        sliced = m.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, 0], plane_normal=[0, 1, 0])
        if sliced is not None:
            # convert to 2D
            slice_2d, _ = sliced.to_2D()
            for poly in slice_2d.polygons_full:
                ax.fill(*poly.exterior.xy, facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5)
                for interior in poly.interiors:
                    ax.fill(*interior.xy, facecolor='white', edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5)
    except Exception:
        # fallback: silhouette
        v = m.vertices
        ax.fill(v[:, 0], v[:, 2], facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.1, alpha=0.2)
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Z (mm)'); ax.set_title('Section through Y=0 (inside view)')
ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Top view (X-Y, looking down)
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 3)
for name, m, color in scene_meshes:
    # project to X-Y by drawing outlines at multiple Z slices
    # simpler: just outline the vertices in X-Y
    v = m.vertices
    # convex hull in xy as a footprint approximation
    try:
        from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull
        pts = v[:, :2]
        hull = ConvexHull(pts)
        ax.fill(pts[hull.vertices, 0], pts[hull.vertices, 1],
                facecolor=color, edgecolor='k', alpha=0.3, label=name)
    except Exception:
        pass
ax.set_xlabel('X (mm)'); ax.set_ylabel('Y (mm)'); ax.set_title('Top view (footprints)')
ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(loc='upper right')

# Dimensions text panel
ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 4)
ax.axis('off')
info = f"""IMPULSE JIG — design summary

Mass:          {total_mass_g} g  ({weight_count}× {weight_unit_mass_g} g fishing weights)
Drop height:   {drop_height_mm} mm
Impact vel:    {v_impact_ms:.2f} m/s
Energy:        {ke_J:.3f} J

TUBE
  ID:          {tube_id_mm} mm  (puck OD + {2*puck_clearance_mm} mm clearance)
  OD:          {tube_od_mm} mm
  Height:      {tube_total_height_mm} mm  (drop + 30 mm headroom)
  Base plate:  {base_dia_mm} mm dia × {base_thickness_mm} mm thick

PUCK
  OD:          {puck_outer_dia_mm} mm
  ID:          {puck_inner_dia_mm} mm
  Height:      {puck_total_height_mm:.1f} mm
  Bottom:      {puck_bottom_mm} mm SOLID (striking face)

CAP
  OD:          {puck_outer_dia_mm} mm
  Lip dia:     {puck_inner_dia_mm - 2*cap_clearance_mm:.2f} mm (friction fit)
  Lip depth:   {cap_lip_height_mm} mm

PIN
  Dia:         {pin_dia_mm} mm (hole {pin_dia_mm+0.3} mm for paperclip)
  Z position:  {drop_height_mm} mm above tube interior bottom

PRINT SETTINGS
  Tube:  vertical on plate, 4 walls, 30% gyroid, 100% on base
  Puck:  open-face up, 4 walls, 100% bottom
  Cap:   flange-down, 4 walls
"""
ax.text(0.02, 0.98, info, family='monospace', fontsize=10, va='top', ha='left')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, 'jig_preview.png'), dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
print(f"  saved jig_preview.png")
print("\nDone.")

content.text:
Regenerated and pushed (9178c5a). Key change for X1C compatibility:

| Spec | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tube total height | 264 mm | **250 mm** |
| X1C Z margin | -8 mm (over!) | **+6 mm** |
| Loading funnel at top | none | **5 mm chamfer, ID widens 27→32 mm** |
| Drop height | 230 mm | 230 mm (unchanged) |
| Impact energy | 0.27 J | 0.27 J (unchanged) |

## What changed in the design

The tube no longer encloses the entire puck when loaded. When the puck rests on the pin:
- Its lower 16 mm is inside the tube (guided alignment)
- Its upper ~22 mm sticks above the tube top

This is functionally fine because the puck only needs lateral guidance until it accelerates downward — at which point it's well inside the tube and stays guided through the full drop. The new loading funnel at the top makes inserting the puck onto the pin straightforward.

## Bambu X1C print plan

All three parts on one plate, single PLA spool:

| Part | Orientation | Layer | Walls | Infill | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tube | vertical (long axis = Z) | 0.20 mm | 4 | 30% gyroid | ~3 hr |
| Puck | open face up | 0.16 mm | 4 | 100% | ~30 min |
| Cap | flange-side down | 0.20 mm | 4 | 100% | ~10 min |

**~3.5 hr total** (mostly the tube). Bambu Studio's auto-arrange handles the layout.

Recommend: **5 mm brim on the tube** for adhesion stability — it's a 250 mm tall thin print with a 33 mm OD footprint, so any wobble during print propagates. Brim eliminates that risk.

The `.scad` file has all the print-setting notes baked in as comments. If you ever want to change drop height, weight count, or printer max-Z target, edit the parameters at the top and re-render — total height auto-recomputes with an X1C margin check.

not acceptable because the result is fit quantitatively.

### Phase B — Sim-correction data (15–30 min)

Each event in this phase is **labeled in a separate paper / phone log**
with timestamp, class, distance, and any anomaly (bounce off wall, wet
floor, etc.).

| Event class | Count target | Distances | Notes |
|-------------|--------------|-----------|-------|
| Object drop — water bottle | 15 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 5 each | Rigid, single-impact-with-rebound class. Drops from waist height (~1 m). |
| Object drop — phone | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × ~3 each | Lower-mass rigid object. Same drop height. |
| Object drop — glass | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | Brittle / multi-impact class. Drops from waist height. Be careful. |
| Catfood-bag drop (body-fall surrogate) | 30 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m × 10 each | At 1.5 m, split 5 with operator between drop and sensor ("body in path") and 5 without |
| Slow-slump surrogate | 10 | 0.5 / 1.5 / 2.5 m | Heavy bag (~10 kg) lowered slowly onto floor; controlled descent, not free fall |
| Step / walk (extra, beyond A5) | continuous 5 min | n/a | Operator walks varied paths; oversample for cadence statistics |
| Confuser — shower running | 60 s | n/a | Continuous, separately recorded |
| Confuser — vent on | 60 s | n/a | Continuous |
| Confuser — toilet flush | 5 flushes | n/a | One file with 5 distinct flushes |
| Confuser — washer (if present) | 60 s + a spin-up | n/a | Skip if not in/adjacent to bathroom |

Save Phase B events grouped by class:
```
<bathroom_id>_drop_water_<date>.csv      # all water drops in one file
<bathroom_id>_drop_phone_<date>.csv

```

### Logging discipline

For every event in Phase B:
- Note timestamp (CSV records its own; phone log records wall clock for
  cross-reference)
- Event class label
- Distance from sensor (m)
- Body-in-path? (yes/no) — relevant for catfood-bag drops at 1.5 m
- Surface state (wet/dry)
- Any anomaly

A handwritten or phone-notes log with timestamps is sufficient. Goal:
ability to retro-label each event in the CSV during post-processing.
